## Not Every Cheap House in Japan Is an Abandoned Akiya

Stories about free houses in Japan usually show wrecks. These 18 homes start at €18,400 and you could move into them.

RealHunt Research · 2026-09-23

You have probably seen the headlines: Japan has millions of empty houses, and some towns give them away. It is true. It is also why so many people are disappointed when they look closer. Most of the free and near-free houses need a new roof, new plumbing and months of work, and some are not worth saving.

So we set a different bar. The 18 Japanese homes on RealHunt all look like somewhere you could live now. Prices start at €18,400 and the middle of the list is €51,980.

[€54,280 · Hillside kominka with sea views over the Kyoto coastMaizuru, Kyoto, Japan](https://realhunt.co/deal/Da7vZIFDIuo)

### What the money buys

At the bottom of the range you get older wooden houses in the countryside: a 100-year-old farmhouse with its own farmland, or a 1977 single-storey house with a sakura garden in Usuki, Oita, about 500 metres from the sea. Around €40,000 to €60,000 the houses are often renovated, with new kitchens and bathrooms, and several have sea views on the Seto Inland Sea or the Sea of Japan coast.

[€19,320 · Japanese home with a sakura gardenUsuki, Oita, Japan](https://realhunt.co/deal/DbbD15oDKLz)[€56,120 · Freshly renovated five-bedroom house with an ocean viewKashiwazaki, Niigata, Japan](https://realhunt.co/deal/DcTSbXtj9qu)[€57,040 · Renovated island house with one of Japan's best sea viewsKojima, Okayama, Japan](https://realhunt.co/deal/Db59YYrjN5h)

At the top, around €91,000, there is a Japanese-style single-storey house with an engawa (the wooden veranda) and a garden in Yugawara, a coastal hot spring town about 90 minutes from Tokyo.

### Can a foreigner buy?

Yes. Japan lets foreigners own houses and land outright, with no visa or residency needed to buy. Buying costs add up to roughly 8% on top of the price: acquisition tax, registration, stamp duty and the agent's commission, which is capped by law. Owning a house does not give you a visa, so if you want to live there full time that is a separate question.

### What to check

Age matters in Japan in a way it does not in Europe. Houses built before June 1981 were built to older earthquake rules. Many are fine and some have been reinforced, but ask. Ask too about the septic system, whether the land is freehold or leased, and what the fixed asset tax is each year (usually low for older rural houses).

Distance is the other thing. A house in a quiet coastal town can be two or three hours from a big city by train. That is the point for some buyers and a problem for others.

## Cheap Houses in Sweden: What €22,000 to €99,000 Gets You

41 Swedish homes under €100,000, most of them red wooden houses on big plots near a lake. Where they are, what they cost to buy, and what to check.

RealHunt Research · 2026-09-23

Sweden is the country people are most surprised by when they browse RealHunt. It has a reputation for being expensive, and in Stockholm it is. But 41 of the homes on our site are Swedish, all under €100,000, and most of them look like the picture you have in your head: a red wooden house with white corners, a garden, and a lake somewhere behind the trees.

[€57,000 · Classic red Swedish house with gardens and berry bushesNordmark, Värmland, Sweden](https://realhunt.co/deal/DbjsJpRGdDa)

### Where the cheap ones are

Värmland, in the west near the Norwegian border, has the most homes on our list. After that come Småland, Dalarna, Skåne and Jönköping. These are forest and lake regions with small towns, not suburbs. Many houses are an hour or so from an airport: Karlstad, Växjö, Jönköping or Göteborg depending on where you are.

The cheapest Swedish home on the site is €22,000, a wooden house in the forest 550 metres from a lake. The median is €72,000. For that you usually get a detached house with a plot measured in thousands of square metres, not hundreds. Several come with a sauna, a guest cabin or a barn.

[€22,000 · Charming wooden house in the forest near a lakeCentral Sweden](https://realhunt.co/deal/Dc6j54PF6hV)[€72,000 · Off-grid lakefront cottage with own jetty and wood-fired saunaSunnemo, Värmland, Sweden](https://realhunt.co/deal/DccwxoxINB2)[€64,000 · Sea-view cabin with swimming access and boat mooringHornön, Västernorrland, Sweden](https://realhunt.co/deal/DdP0Csyilzz)

### How buying works

This is where Sweden is easy. Anyone can buy a house, whether or not you live in the EU. There is no notary. The buyer pays a stamp duty (lagfart) of 1.5% of the price plus a small fixed fee to register the title, and a mortgage registration fee if you borrow. The seller pays the estate agent. On a €60,000 house your buying costs are roughly €1,000 to €2,000.

Sales usually run as open bidding through the agent. The asking price is a starting point, and popular houses can go above it. You sign a contract, pay a deposit of around 10%, and the rest on the day you get the keys.

### What to check before you bid

Winter. Ask what heating the house has (wood, electric, a heat pump or geothermal) and what it cost to heat last winter. Several homes on our list mention geothermal or heat pumps, which bring the bills down a lot.

Water and drains. Country houses often have their own well and septic system. Ask when the septic tank was last emptied and whether the well water has been tested.

Access. A gravel road that is lovely in June can be hard work in January. Ask who clears the snow.

In Sweden the buyer is expected to inspect the house properly before buying, and hidden faults you could have found are usually your problem afterwards. Many sellers order an inspection report; read it, even with a translator, and consider your own.

## Why We Say No to Most Cheap Houses

A cheap house that needs €80,000 of work is not a cheap house. The rule we use to decide what goes on RealHunt, and why we turn most listings down.

RealHunt Research · 2026-09-23

The internet is full of cheap houses. Most of them are cheap for a reason. The €1 houses in Italian villages come with an obligation to renovate, usually within three years, and the renovation costs far more than €1. The Japanese akiya you see in videos often need new roofs. And a lot of the American homes under $50,000 are listed for investors because they are not fit to live in.

RealHunt is for a different question: what can you buy for under €100,000 and live in, more or less as it is?

### The rule

Every home is looked at by a person before it goes up. We say no to:

- homes that clearly need major work: a new roof, rebuilt walls, no kitchen or bathroom
- ruins and shells, however pretty the stone
- land on its own, or land with a trailer or a shed
- listings with one photo, or photos of the town instead of the house
- anything over €100,000

Old is fine. Some of our favourite homes were built in the 1800s. What matters is that someone has looked after them.

In practice this means we turn down far more than we publish. We turn down about three listings for every one we publish.

[€75,000 · Fully renovated, fully furnished stone home in a quiet Tuscan villageSubbiano, Arezzo, Tuscany, Italy](https://realhunt.co/deal/Dc8Edq5j8H_)

### Where the homes come from

Some are found by our own research on public listing sites. Some come from people and accounts who post homes they have found, and every one goes through the same check. Signed-in members can open the original listing and contact the seller or agent directly. RealHunt is not an estate agent and does not sell the houses.

### How the ranking works

Every home that passes gets a grade from 70 to 98, built from 11 sub-scores: price, price per m², space, condition, extras, water, weather, airport, buying costs, listing detail and buyer interest. The front page, the country pages and the price lists are ordered by that grade, best first. Votes and saves only move the buyer-interest sub-score. [How the score works](https://realhunt.co/method). There are no paid placements in the ranking. Where there is a sponsored card, it says so.

### What we get wrong

Photos can flatter. Listings go out of date. A house that looks fine may have a problem only a survey will find. If you see a home that is sold or not what it seems, use the report button on its page and we will check it. And before you buy anything, anywhere, get an independent inspection and a local lawyer or notary.

[See the best homes](https://realhunt.co/)

## Italian Homes Near the Sea for Under €50,000: Where They Actually Are

Cheap Italian houses are usually in inland hill towns. A few are close to the water. Here is where they are and what the catch is.

RealHunt Research · 2026-09-23

Most of the cheap Italian homes you see online are in inland villages, and there is a reason: the coast is where Italians go on holiday, so that is where prices are high. But not everywhere. On RealHunt right now there are a handful of homes under €50,000 that are on the coast or a few minutes' drive from a beach, and they cluster in three places: Calabria, Sicily and Puglia.

[€39,000 · Sea-view terrace in Acquappesa, CalabriaAcquappesa, Cosenza, Calabria, Italy](https://realhunt.co/deal/acquappesa-sea-view-39000)

### Calabria

The toe of Italy has the longest coastline of any mainland region and some of the lowest prices. In Acquappesa, on the Tyrrhenian side, there is a one-bedroom place with a sea-view terrace for €39,000, about 2 km from the water. Further south in Falconara Albanese there is a three-room flat with a sea view for €41,000. Two more homes in Calabria, at €30,000 and €35,000, are listed as five minutes from the beach.

[€41,000 · Apartment with sea view in Falconara Albanese, CosenzaFalconara Albanese, Cosenza, Italy](https://realhunt.co/deal/falconara-albanese-41000)[€30,000 · Sea-view house five minutes from the beachCalabria, Italy](https://realhunt.co/deal/Dcgta8yjCAR)[€35,000 · Sea-view house five minutes from the beachCalabria, Italy](https://realhunt.co/deal/Dc32k2tDKLf)

### Sicily

In Marsala, on the west coast, a 135 m² apartment is €34,000, about 600 metres from the sea. That is €252 per square metre, the lowest on the site for an Italian home with a size in the listing. In Acquedolci, on the north coast near Messina, a two-level flat that was largely renovated is €49,000. There is also a sea-view home with an 87 m² panoramic terrace 20 minutes from Messina for the same price.

[€34,000 · Apartment in Marsala, TrapaniMarsala, Trapani, Italy](https://realhunt.co/deal/marsala-34000)[€49,000 · Duplex in Acquedolci, MessinaAcquedolci, Messina, Italy](https://realhunt.co/deal/acquedolci-49000)[€49,000 · Sea-view home with a panoramic terraceSicily, Italy](https://realhunt.co/deal/Dclv5CJDdhi)

### Puglia and Sardinia

Puglia has two whitewashed and vaulted houses around 20 to 25 minutes from the beach at €28,000 and €49,000. In Sardinia, a furnished tower house on four floors in a historic district is €35,000, about 3 km from the beaches.

### The catch

These are mostly apartments or small village houses, not villas. Sea views at this price usually come with stairs, a small kitchen and a building that has seen a few decades. Summer is busy and some coastal towns are very quiet from November to March. And the costs of buying in Italy are high: plan for 10% on top, plus about €2,500 in fees.

Always ask for the APE (the energy certificate) and whether the property is "conforme": that what is built matches what is registered at the land registry. A good local geometra can check this for a few hundred euros, and it is worth every one.

All of them in one place: [cheap houses by the sea in Italy](https://realhunt.co/cheap-houses/by-the-sea-in-italy). For the hill towns, see [stone houses in Italy](https://realhunt.co/cheap-houses/stone-houses-in-italy).

## How Many Months of Rent Would Buy You a Whole House?

We divided the median price of homes on RealHunt by three monthly rents. At €1,200 a month, a typical Italian village house costs less than three years of rent.

RealHunt Research · 2026-09-23

This is the comparison that surprises people most. If you pay €1,200 a month in rent, you hand over €14,400 a year. In three years that is €43,200, which is more than the median price of an Italian home on our site (€41,000).

That does not mean you should quit your lease tomorrow. A house in a village two hours from the nearest city is not the same thing as a flat near your job. But the comparison is useful because it puts a price you cannot picture (a house in another country) next to one you pay every month.

### The table

We took the median price of the homes published on RealHunt in each country and divided it by three monthly rents: €800, €1,200 and €2,000. We did not use official rent figures for any city. Pick the column closest to what you pay.

Country | Median home on RealHunt | Months at €800 | Months at €1,200 | Months at €2,000
Italy | €41,000 | 51 | 34 | 20
Japan | €51,980 | 65 | 43 | 26
Sweden | €72,000 | 90 | 60 | 36
Mexico | €80,920 | 101 | 67 | 40
United States | €85,929 | 107 | 72 | 43
Canada | €92,552 | 116 | 77 | 46

Across all 140 homes the median is €61,280. At €1,200 a month that is 51 months of rent, a little over four years.

### What the table leaves out

Buying costs come first. They range from about 2% of the price in Sweden to about 10% in Italy, plus fixed fees. On each home page we show the estimate for that exact price.

Then there is the cost of keeping a house. Council tax on a small Italian village home is often a few hundred euros a year. In Sweden and Canada, heating in winter is the big one. In the US, property tax is set by the county and is usually shown in the listing. None of this is close to rent, but it is not zero.

And there is the part no spreadsheet captures: whether you actually want to live there. The cheapest homes are cheap because people left those places. Some are coming back to life with remote workers and retirees; others are quiet for a reason. Visit before you buy. Stay a week, in winter if you can.

### Try it with your own rent

On every home page on RealHunt there is a line that says how many months of rent the house is worth. It uses a rough average rent for the city your browser is in. It is a nudge, not financial advice, but it is a fair way to see these prices.

[€16,000 · Two-bedroom apartment with terrace in a historic Tuscan villageMontieri, Grosseto, Tuscany, Italy](https://realhunt.co/deal/DdSm-JkiJem)[€16,000 · Two-bedroom apartment with two balconies in a historic villageFiamignano, Rieti, Lazio, Italy](https://realhunt.co/deal/Dcsm9sZoDMp)[€19,320 · Japanese home with a sakura gardenUsuki, Oita, Japan](https://realhunt.co/deal/DbbD15oDKLz)

## Move-In-Ready Houses in the US for Around $100,000

We published 13 US homes that cost under €100,000 and do not need gutting. They start at $75,000. Here is where they are.

RealHunt Research · 2026-09-23

Search for cheap houses in the US and you find thousands under $100,000. Open them and many are the same story: fire damage, boarded windows, "cash only, investor special". We went through them looking for the opposite, homes you could move into this month, and published 13 so far.

They are asking between $75,000 and $110,000. On RealHunt every price is in euros so homes in different countries can be compared; at the rate we used, that is €65,428 to €95,961.

### Where they are

The Pittsburgh area comes up more than anywhere else. McKees Rocks, McKeesport and Clairton, old steel towns along the rivers, have brick houses from the early 1900s with updated kitchens for $75,000 to $98,500. [€78,426 · Updated 3-bed house in Huntington, West VirginiaHuntington, West Virginia](https://realhunt.co/deal/huntington-78426)[€82,875 · Move-in ready 2-bed house in Chapmanville, West VirginiaChapmanville, West Virginia](https://realhunt.co/deal/chapmanville-82875)[€85,929 · Updated 3-bed house in Clairton, PennsylvaniaClairton, Pennsylvania](https://realhunt.co/deal/clairton-85929)

### What "move-in ready" means here

We only publish a US home if the photos show a kitchen and bathroom in working order, floors, walls and windows in good shape, and no sign of major damage. It is not an inspection. It is a first filter so you do not waste an afternoon on a house with a hole in the roof.

### Buying as a foreigner

Anyone can buy a house in the US. You do not need residency or a visa. Buyer closing costs are usually 2% to 5% of the price: title insurance, escrow and recording fees. Property tax is charged every year by the county or town, often somewhere between 0.5% and 2% of the assessed value, and the listing usually shows it. Owning a home does not give you the right to live in the US; that is a separate visa question.

### What to check

Get a home inspection. Ask about the age of the roof, the furnace and the water heater, which are the big bills in the first years. Check flood zone maps for houses near rivers. And look at the street on a map: in some of these towns, prices can change a lot from one block to the next.

See them all: [homes in the United States](https://realhunt.co/homes/united-states).

## How to spot a property scam when you buy a house abroad

The warning signs we see in cheap-house listings, and six checks that stop most scams before you send any money.

RealHunt Research · 2026-10-23

Cheap houses attract buyers from far away, and that is exactly what scammers count on: you cannot easily visit, you do not know the local rules, and a good price makes you want to move fast.

### Warning signs

- The price is far below every similar home in the same town, with no reason given (ruin, auction, shared ownership).

- The "owner" lives abroad, cannot show the house and asks you to pay a deposit to "reserve" it.

- You are asked to pay by bank transfer to a personal account, by crypto, or through a money-transfer service.

- The photos appear on other listings with a different address or price. A reverse image search takes a minute.

- Pressure: "three other buyers are interested", "the offer ends today".

- No land-registry or cadastral reference, or the seller refuses to give one.

### Six checks before you pay anything

- Get the registry extract. In Spain the nota simple, in Italy the visura catastale, in France the extrait cadastral. It shows who owns the house and whether there are debts on it.

- Check the owner's name matches the seller. If an agent sells, ask for the signed mandate from the owner.

- Use your own lawyer or notary, not one recommended by the seller.

- Pay only into an escrow or a notary's client account, never to a person.

- Visit, or send someone. A local surveyor or a video call walking through every room is enough to prove the house exists and matches the photos.

- Read the reservation contract before you sign: what happens to your deposit if the sale fails.

### What RealHunt does

A person checks every home before it goes up, and we link to the original listing so you deal with the real seller or agent. That is not a guarantee: if something on a listing looks wrong, use the report button on its page and we check it.

This is general information, not legal advice. Before you buy, get a local lawyer or notary.

### Where they are

Doral (two homes) is the business and family district west of Miami Airport, with good schools, CityPlace and big parks. Downtown Hollywood (two) is walkable, between Young Circle, Hollywood Boulevard and the beach, about 25 minutes from Miami. Pembroke Pines and Miramar (three, all on lakes) are quiet, green Broward suburbs with good schools, 30 minutes from Miami. Plantation (two) is leafy central Broward next to Fort Lauderdale. Kendall (one) is the established south-west Miami suburb, in a guard-gated community on a lake.

### What they really cost every month

In Florida the cheap price is only half the story, so every home page on RealHunt shows the monthly costs in large type:

- Community fee (HOA). Condos and townhouses pay one every month, often $400 to $900, sometimes including water, cable or building insurance. Two of these listings state it ($625 in Doral and $135 in Miramar); for the others we mark it as not stated, so ask the agent before you visit.

- Property tax. Florida resets the taxable value when a home sells. Listings show what the seller pays, often with a homestead discount; a new owner pays about 1.8% of the price, roughly $4,400 to $5,400 a year for these homes.

- Older condo buildings. Since 2022 Florida requires older condo buildings to pass structural inspections and keep repair reserves, which has led to large special assessments in some towers. We avoided any listing that mentioned one, but ask for the latest inspection, the reserve study and the board minutes before you make an offer.

- Insurance. Home insurance is extra. Impact windows, like those in the two Westview townhouses, lower it.

### How we chose them

We started from every active listing in Hallandale Beach, Hollywood, Pembroke Pines, Miami Lakes, Doral, Kendall, North Bay Village, Sunny Isles Beach, Miramar and Plantation, kept 2 and 3-bedroom homes from $170,000 to $300,000 (858 homes), checked fees, year built and red flags for the most promising 193, then looked at the photos of the last 16. Six more were dropped for dark, empty or virtually staged rooms. The score is RealHunt's usual one: price for the area, condition, location and what is nearby.

## What to check when you visit a cheap house: a 20-point checklist

Roof, damp, water, power, access, paperwork: the things that turn a cheap house into an expensive one, and how to check them in one visit.

RealHunt Research · 2026-10-23

Most cheap houses are cheap because of something you can see on a visit, if you know where to look. Take this list with you, or send it to the person who visits for you.

### Outside

- Roof: missing or slipped tiles, sagging lines, stains on the ceiling below.

- Walls: cracks wider than a coin, especially diagonal ones from window corners.

- Damp: a white salt line or flaking paint at the bottom of walls.

- Drainage: where rain water goes, and whether the ground slopes toward the house.

- Access: can a car or a van reach the door all year? Who owns the track?

- Boundaries: does the plot on the ground match the plot on the cadastral map?

### Inside

- Smell: a musty smell means damp, even if the walls were just painted.

- Electricity: age of the fuse box, earthing, whether the supply is connected or cut off.

- Water: mains, well or tank; pressure at the top tap; hot water.

- Waste water: mains sewer or septic tank, and whether the tank meets current rules.

- Heating: what kind, what it costs a winter, and whether the chimney works.

- Windows: single or double glazing, rot in wooden frames.

- Floors: soft spots, slopes, woodworm holes in beams.

- Kitchen and bathroom: usable now, or a full rebuild?

### Around

- Phone signal and internet: test it in the house, not in the village square.

- Noise: visit once on a weekday and once in the evening if you can.

- Neighbours: empty houses next door can mean damp or structural problems shared through walls.

- Services: nearest shop, doctor and pharmacy, and how long the drive is in winter.

### Paperwork

- The registry extract matches the house you saw: rooms, size, outbuildings. Unregistered extensions can be a problem when you sell.

- Energy certificate, and any pending local taxes or community fees.

If several of these need work, get a quote before you make an offer: it is your best argument for a lower price. RealHunt's [help buying](https://realhunt.co/help-buying) page lists local surveyors and lawyers.

## What €50,000 Buys in 2026: 140 Checked Homes, Country by Country

We sorted every home on RealHunt by price. 46 of 140 cost €50,000 or less, and almost all of them are in three countries.

RealHunt Research · 2026-09-23

€50,000 is roughly what a new mid-size car costs, or a deposit on a flat in most European cities. We wanted to know what it buys if you spend it on a whole house instead, so we sorted every home currently published on RealHunt by price.

The short answer: 46 of the 140 homes on the site cost €50,000 or less. They are not spread evenly. 29 are in Italy, 9 in Japan and 6 in Sweden. France and Denmark have one each. Spain, the United States, Canada and Mexico have none under that line.

Every home here passed the same check: a person looked at the photos and the listing, and anything that needs a new roof, is a ruin, is only land or has a single photo was left out. So these are cheap homes you could sleep in, not projects.

### Italy: the most homes for the money

Italy has the cheapest home on the site, a stone house in a Lazio hill town for €12,000, about 55 minutes from Rome's Ciampino airport. Half of the 39 Italian homes cost €41,000 or less. At this price you are mostly buying in small inland villages: Tuscany, Lazio, Umbria and Abruzzo come up again and again. Expect thick stone walls, a small kitchen, and a piazza five minutes away on foot.

[€12,000 · Stone house in a hill town 55 min from RomeLazio, Italy](https://realhunt.co/deal/DcoUnwBDDxF)[€13,000 · Stone-village home near Viterbo, 1h30 from RomeGrotte Santo Stefano, Viterbo, Lazio, Italy](https://realhunt.co/deal/grotte-santo-stefano-13000)[€16,000 · Two-bedroom apartment with terrace in a historic Tuscan villageMontieri, Grosseto, Tuscany, Italy](https://realhunt.co/deal/DdSm-JkiJem)

What the price hides: Italy's buying costs are the highest on our list. For a second home, registration tax is 9% of the cadastral value (a tax value that is usually well below the price), and the notary and registry add about €2,500. Our cost estimate adds roughly 10% plus €2,500 to be safe, so a €30,000 house is closer to €35,500 all in.

### Japan: bigger houses, lower running costs

Japan's cheapest homes on RealHunt start at €18,400 and the middle of the list is €51,980. 9 of 18 are under €50,000. For that money the houses tend to be larger than in Italy, often with a garden, and many are near the coast in Wakayama, Kyoto prefecture and Okayama. Foreigners can own land and houses outright in Japan, with no residency needed to buy.

[€19,320 · Japanese home with a sakura gardenUsuki, Oita, Japan](https://realhunt.co/deal/DbbD15oDKLz)[€34,960 · Single-storey Japanese house in a seaside townKainan, Wakayama, Japan](https://realhunt.co/deal/DdJ6Zs_DcnX)[€43,240 · Single-storey house with a huge lawn on the Seto Inland SeaMitoyo, Kagawa, Japan](https://realhunt.co/deal/DdWPFmBkdhr)

### Sweden: where €50,000 is the entry ticket

Sweden's median on our list is €72,000, higher than Italy or Japan, and only 6 of 41 Swedish homes are under €50,000. But what you get is often a detached wooden house with a big plot, near a lake, with a wood stove. Anyone can buy in Sweden, and the only real buying cost is a 1.5% stamp duty. There is no notary.

[€22,000 · Charming wooden house in the forest near a lakeCentral Sweden](https://realhunt.co/deal/Dc6j54PF6hV)[€25,960 · Cosy villa with sauna, 100 m from the riverNorthern Sweden](https://realhunt.co/deal/DdPBLT2CLlb)[€36,000 · Cosy Dalarna cottage with guest cottage and pergolaStensbo, Dalarna, Sweden](https://realhunt.co/deal/Dc2FknAIzJt)

### North America starts higher

In the United States the cheapest move-in-ready home we have published is €65,428 (a brick row house in McKees Rocks, Pennsylvania, asking $75,000). Canada starts at €55,842 and Mexico at €50,575. Those markets have plenty of cheaper listings, but at the very bottom many are sold as investor projects: boarded windows, fire damage, or a plot with a trailer on it. They do not pass our quality rule.

### What we take from this

If €50,000 is your hard ceiling, Italy is where you will have the most choice by far, Japan is where you get the most house, and Sweden is where you get the most land. Add 2% (Sweden) to 10% (Italy) on top for taxes and fees, and always pay for a survey before you sign.

You can see every home under €50,000 on one page: [houses for sale under €50,000](https://realhunt.co/cheap-houses/under-50000), or just [the ones under €30,000](https://realhunt.co/cheap-houses/under-30000).

## Bulgaria vs Canada: where is a cheap home better value?

On RealHunt, homes in Bulgaria cost a median €740 per m², 20% less than in Canada (€930 per m²). Buying costs start at about 3.2% in Bulgaria and 1.5% in Canada.

| Bulgaria | Canada
Homes on RealHunt | 6 | 9
Median price | €66,000 | €92,552
Median price per m² | €740 | €930
Cheapest home | €58,900 | €55,842
Median score | 93 | 86
Costs on top of the price | 3.2-8.5% | 1.5-4%
Can foreigners buy? | Yes, buildings and apartments, with rights similar to locals; per GPG, foreigners can't own land directly, so a Bulgarian company is the usual route. | Mostly not for now: a federal ban stops non-Canadians from buying homes in cities and larger towns until January 1, 2027, with exceptions such as work permit holders and spouses of citizens or permanent residents. The ban does not cover rural areas and small towns, and the government has said it does not plan simply to extend it, but a replacement is being studied.
Yearly property tax | 0.01-0.45% of the property's tax value plus a municipal garbage fee. | Property tax is set by each city as a share of assessed value, from about 0.3% in Vancouver to 2.12% in Saint John in 2026.
Tax on rental income | Non-residents: 10% final tax on gross rent, paid quarterly, no deductions. | Non-residents have 25% of gross rent withheld, but they can file a Section 216 return to pay tax on net rent instead, and Form NR6 lets the agent withhold on net rent.

Prices describe the homes on RealHunt, each checked by a person, not every home in each country. Rules and taxes: general information, not legal or tax advice.

## Bulgaria vs Cyprus: where is a cheap home better value?

On RealHunt, homes in Bulgaria cost a median €740 per m², 82% less than in Cyprus (€4,060 per m²). Buying costs start at about 3.2% in Bulgaria and 2.5% in Cyprus.

| Bulgaria | Cyprus
Homes on RealHunt | 6 | 3
Median price | €66,000 | €350,000
Median price per m² | €740 | €4,060
Cheapest home | €58,900 | €341,000
Median score | 93 | 92
Costs on top of the price | 3.2-8.5% | 2.5-3.5%
Can foreigners buy? | Yes, buildings and apartments, with rights similar to locals; per GPG, foreigners can't own land directly, so a Bulgarian company is the usual route. | EU citizens buy without restrictions. Non-EU buyers need permission from the Council of Ministers, applied for through the District Officer, and are normally limited to one home or a plot of up to 4,014 m².

## Buying costs in Albania

About 1.3-1.9% on top of the price in taxes and fees. Use the calculator on this page for your price, or see the worked examples:

### Worked examples

Price | Taxes and fees | Total
€150,000 | €1,950 to €2,850 | €151,950 to €152,850
€300,000 | €3,900 to €5,700 | €303,900 to €305,700

### Where the money goes

Notary 0.23-0.35% + lawyer 0.1-0.5% + agent 1-2%; transfer tax (0.5-3%) is paid by the seller (GPG, 2021).

### Every year after you buy

Yearly property tax: Local property tax ~0.05% of cadastral value (about EUR 75/yr on EUR 150k).

Tax on rental income: Flat 15% on rental income, including short-term, declared via the DIVA platform.

Costs are a share of the price, so they work in any currency. Figures as of 2026. General information, not tax or legal advice.

## Buying costs in Bali

About 6.5-18% on top of the price in taxes and fees. Use the calculator on this page for your price, or see the worked examples:

Price | Taxes and fees | Total
€150,000 | €9,750 to €27,000 | €159,750 to €177,000

### Where the money goes

BPHTB transfer tax 5% + notary 1-2.5% + legal 0.5-1.5% (GPG: 6.5-9%); new developer units add 11% PPN/VAT (stack ~17-18% without the 2026 PPN-DTP incentive, ~6-9% with it). Plain leasehold deals mostly notary/legal.

## Buying costs in Canada

About 1.5-4% on top of the price in taxes and fees. Use the calculator on this page for your price, or see the worked examples:

### Worked examples

Price | Taxes and fees | Total
€150,000 | €2,250 to €6,000 | €152,250 to €156,000
€300,000 | €4,500 to €12,000 | €304,500 to €312,000

### Where the money goes

Buyers usually pay provincial land transfer tax on a sliding scale (Ontario: 0.5% up to $55,000 and 1% from $55,000 to $250,000), legal fees of about $500 to $1,500, title insurance of about $250 and an inspection of $300 to $1,000, while the seller usually pays the agents; foreign buyers also pay Ontario's 25% non-resident speculation tax anywhere in Ontario and British Columbia's 20% additional tax in Metro Vancouver and four other regions.

### Every year after you buy

Yearly property tax: Property tax is set by each city as a share of assessed value, from about 0.3% in Vancouver to 2.12% in Saint John in 2026.

Tax on rental income: Non-residents have 25% of gross rent withheld, but they can file a Section 216 return to pay tax on net rent instead, and Form NR6 lets the agent withhold on net rent.

## Buying costs in Cyprus

About 2.5-3.5% on top of the price in taxes and fees. Use the calculator on this page for your price, or see the worked examples:

€300,000 | €7,500 to €10,500 | €307,500 to €310,500

### Where the money goes

Land Registry transfer fees of 3% up to €85,000, 5% to €170,000 and 8% above, halved for resales without VAT (1.5%, 2.5% and 4%); stamp duty abolished from 1 January 2026; lawyer about 1% plus VAT; small Land Registry charges.

### Every year after you buy

Yearly property tax: There is no annual national property tax (abolished in 2017); owners pay municipal fees of about €90 to €300 a year, plus sewerage and local authority charges.

Tax on rental income: Non-residents pay income tax on Cyprus rental income at 20% to 35% after deducting 20% of the gross rent and loan interest, plus a 2.65% health contribution (GHS); the special defence contribution does not apply to them.

## Buying costs in Denmark

About 1.5-3% on top of the price in taxes and fees. Use the calculator on this page for your price, or see the worked examples:

Price | Taxes and fees | Total
€150,000 | €2,250 to €4,500 | €152,250 to €154,500
€300,000 | €4,500 to €9,000 | €304,500 to €309,000

### Where the money goes

Registration fee on the deed (tinglysningsafgift) of DKK 1,850 plus 0.6% of the price, about 1% for a buyer's lawyer, and, if you borrow, a mortgage registration fee of DKK 1,825 plus 1.25% of the loan; the seller normally pays the agent.

### Every year after you buy

Yearly property tax: Owners pay property value tax (ejendomsværdiskat) of 0.51% on 80% of the official valuation (1.4% above DKK 9.2 million) plus municipal land tax (grundskyld) at a rate set by each municipality, capped at 30 per mille of the land value.

Tax on rental income: A non-resident who rents out a Danish home is taxed in Denmark on the profit under the ordinary Danish rules; staying in Denmark more than 3 months at a time or 180 days a year, or working there, makes you fully tax liable.

Costs are a share of the price, so they work in any currency. Figures as of 2026. General information, not tax or legal advice.

## Buying costs in France

About 7-8.5% on top of the price in taxes and fees. Use the calculator on this page for your price, or see the worked examples:

### Worked examples

Price | Taxes and fees | Total
€150,000 | €10,500 to €12,750 | €160,500 to €162,750
€300,000 | €21,000 to €25,500 | €321,000 to €325,500

### Where the money goes

Transfer taxes (droits de mutation) of about 5.8%, or about 6.3% in departments that raised their rate for 2025 to March 2028; notary fee (émoluments) on a sliding scale from 3.87% down to 0.799% plus 20% VAT, about 1.3% on a €150,000 home; land security contribution (contribution de sécurité immobilière) 0.10%; disbursements (débours) of about €800 to €1,200; the agent fee is usually built into the advertised price (FAI) and paid by the seller, sometimes shared.

### Every year after you buy

Yearly property tax: Owners pay an annual property tax (taxe foncière) set by the local authorities, and owners of a furnished second home also pay housing tax (taxe d'habitation), which some communes raise by a surcharge of 5% to 60%.

Tax on rental income: Non-residents pay French income tax on French rental income at a minimum rate of 20% (30% above about €27,500), plus social charges of 17.2%, or 7.5% for people covered by social security in another EU/EEA country or Switzerland.

Costs are a share of the price, so they work in any currency. Figures as of 2026. General information, not tax or legal advice.

Yearly property tax: Only for tax residents: 0.05-1% of value depending on household income; non-residents generally exempt.

Tax on rental income: 5% of gross rent on residential property (long- or short-term), residents and non-residents alike.

Costs are a share of the price, so they work in any currency. Figures as of 2026. General information, not tax or legal advice.

## Buying costs in Germany

About 5-8.5% on top of the price in taxes and fees. Use the calculator on this page for your price, or see the worked examples:

### Worked examples

Price | Taxes and fees | Total
€150,000 | €7,500 to €12,750 | €157,500 to €162,750
€300,000 | €15,000 to €25,500 | €315,000 to €325,500

### Where the money goes

Real estate transfer tax (Grunderwerbsteuer) of 3.5% to 6.5% depending on the state (3.5% in Bavaria, 6.5% in Brandenburg, North Rhine-Westphalia, Saarland and Schleswig-Holstein), plus notary and land registry fees (Notar- und Grundbuchkosten) of about 1.5-2%; if the seller hired the agent, the buyer pays half the commission by law, which is extra.

### Every year after you buy

Yearly property tax: Owners pay property tax (Grundsteuer), calculated since 2025 as assessed value x a tax rate x a municipal multiplier (Hebesatz) that each municipality sets.

Tax on rental income: Non-resident owners are taxed in Germany on net rental income at the normal progressive income tax rates, but without the basic tax-free allowance (Grundfreibetrag).

Costs are a share of the price, so they work in any currency. Figures as of 2026. General information, not tax or legal advice.

Transfer tax 3.09% of the price or the taxable value, whichever is higher; notary about 0.8-1% plus VAT; land registry fees about 0.5-0.7%; lawyer 1-2% plus VAT; if an agent is used, the buyer usually pays a commission of 1-3% plus VAT on top.

## Buying costs in Japan

About 6-9% on top of the price in taxes and fees. Use the calculator on this page for your price, or see the worked examples:

### Worked examples

Price | Taxes and fees | Total
€150,000 | €9,000 to €13,500 | €159,000 to €163,500
€300,000 | €18,000 to €27,000 | €318,000 to €327,000

### Where the money goes

The buyer pays an agent fee capped at 3% plus ¥60,000 plus 10% consumption tax (with a special cap of up to ¥330,000 including tax for cheap vacant homes up to ¥8 million), registration tax of 1.5% on land (until March 2029) and 2% standard on the building, real estate acquisition tax of 3% of assessed value, stamp duty, and a judicial scrivener fee of about ¥100,000 to ¥200,000.

### Every year after you buy

Yearly property tax: Fixed asset tax is 1.4% of the government's assessed value, plus city planning tax of up to 0.3% in urban areas, and small residential plots get a lower tax base.

Tax on rental income: Rent paid to a non-resident is subject to 20.42% withholding (except when an individual rents it as their own home), and the owner must file a tax return each year through a tax representative in Japan to settle the final tax.

Costs are a share of the price, so they work in any currency. Figures as of 2026. General information, not tax or legal advice.

## Buying costs in the Netherlands

About 2-9% on top of the price in taxes and fees. Use the calculator on this page for your price, or see the worked examples:

### Worked examples

Price | Taxes and fees | Total
€150,000 | €3,000 to €13,500 | €153,000 to €163,500
€300,000 | €6,000 to €27,000 | €306,000 to €327,000

### Where the money goes

Transfer tax (overdrachtsbelasting) of 8% if you will not live in the home, such as a buy-to-let or holiday home, or 2% if it becomes your main home; a notary fee for the transfer deed of around EUR 500; Kadaster registration fees; and mortgage costs if you borrow; the seller pays its own agent.

### Every year after you buy

Yearly property tax: Owners pay municipal property tax (onroerendezaakbelasting, OZB) on the official WOZ value, at a rate each municipality sets, which in practice is a per mille figure; tenants of homes do not pay it.

Tax on rental income: Non-residents declare Dutch property in box 3, where tax is 36% on a deemed return of 6% of the property's value in 2026, after a tax-free allowance of EUR 59,357 per person, regardless of actual rent.

Costs are a share of the price, so they work in any currency. Figures as of 2026. General information, not tax or legal advice.

## Buying costs in Norway

About 2.5-3% on top of the price in taxes and fees. Use the calculator on this page for your price, or see the worked examples:

### Worked examples

Price | Taxes and fees | Total
€150,000 | €3,750 to €4,500 | €153,750 to €154,500
€300,000 | €7,500 to €9,000 | €307,500 to €309,000

### Where the money goes

Document duty (dokumentavgift) of 2.5% of market value, a registration fee (tinglysingsgebyr) of NOK 545 for the deed and NOK 545 for any mortgage document; a flat in a housing cooperative (borettslag) has no document duty; the seller normally pays the agent.

### Every year after you buy

Yearly property tax: Some municipalities charge property tax (eiendomsskatt), at most 4 per mille of the value after a reduction of at least 30%, and some also give a basic deduction; many charge nothing.

Tax on rental income: Rental profit is normally taxed at 22%, and the Tax Administration says its rental rules also apply to owners who are tax resident abroad.

Costs are a share of the price, so they work in any currency. Figures as of 2026. General information, not tax or legal advice.

Tax on civil law transactions (PCC) 2% of the value, paid by the buyer within 14 days of the deed; notary fee (taksa notarialna) capped at PLN 1,010 plus 0.4% of the value above PLN 60,000, plus 23% VAT; court fee of PLN 200 to enter ownership in the land register (plus PLN 100 for a new register); optional lawyer about 1%; the agent fee (about 2-3%) depends on the agreement.

Tax on rental income: Private rental income is taxed as a flat lump sum (ryczałt) of 8.5% of revenue up to PLN 100,000 a year and 12.5% above that.

About 1.5-3.5% on top of the price in taxes and fees. Use the calculator on this page for your price, or see the worked examples:

### Worked examples

Price | Taxes and fees | Total
€150,000 | €2,250 to €5,250 | €152,250 to €155,250
€300,000 | €4,500 to €10,500 | €304,500 to €310,500

### Where the money goes

Stamp duty on the title (lagfart) of 1.5% of the price or tax value, whichever is higher, plus a SEK 825 fee; if you borrow and need new mortgage deeds (pantbrev), 2% of their amount plus a SEK 375 fee; optional legal advice; the seller normally pays the agent, and a cooperative flat (bostadsrätt) has no lagfart.

### Every year after you buy

Yearly property tax: Houses pay a municipal property fee (kommunal fastighetsavgift) of SEK 10,425 in 2026, or 0.75% of the tax value if that is lower.

Tax on rental income: Non-resident individuals pay 30% tax on net rental income as capital income; for a private home you can first deduct SEK 40,000 per property and 20% of the rent (the 20% does not apply to a bostadsrätt).

Costs are a share of the price, so they work in any currency. Figures as of 2026. General information, not tax or legal advice.

## Buying costs in the United Kingdom

About 3-9% on top of the price in taxes and fees. Use the calculator on this page for your price, or see the worked examples:

### Worked examples

Price | Taxes and fees | Total
€150,000 | €4,500 to €13,500 | €154,500 to €163,500
€300,000 | €9,000 to €27,000 | €309,000 to €327,000

### Where the money goes

In England and Northern Ireland, Stamp Duty Land Tax (SDLT) is 0% up to £125,000 and 2% from £125,001 to £250,000, plus a 2% surcharge for non-UK residents and a further 5% if you already own a home anywhere, so a non-resident who owns another home pays 7% up to £125,000 and 9% to £250,000; solicitor (conveyancer) about 0.6-1% with a typical minimum of around £2,100 including VAT; Land Registry fee £20 to £230; searches extra; the seller pays the estate agent.

### Every year after you buy

Yearly property tax: Owners or occupiers pay council tax to the local council, and many councils in England charge second homes a premium of up to 100% from April 2025.

Tax on rental income: Non-resident landlords pay UK income tax on rent at 20%, 40% or 45%, with 20% deducted at source by the agent or tenant unless HMRC approves gross payment, and the rates on property income are set to rise to 22%, 42% and 47% from April 2027.

Costs are a share of the price, so they work in any currency. Figures as of 2026. General information, not tax or legal advice.

### Where the money goes

Closing costs vary by state and typically run 2-5% of the loan amount, covering title search and title insurance, recording fees, attorney fees, appraisal and lender fees; since August 2024 the seller no longer has to pay the buyer's agent, so the buyer may pay it unless the seller agrees to; FIRPTA does not apply when you buy but does when a foreigner later sells, with the buyer generally withholding 15% of the sale price.

Tax on rental income: By default a non-resident pays 30% of gross rent (or a lower treaty rate), withheld at source, or can elect to treat the rent as business income and pay graduated rates on net income by filing Form 1040-NR and giving Form W-8ECI to the withholding agent.

## Can an American buy property in Bulgaria?

Short answer: Yes, with conditions.

Yes, with a condition: Americans can own apartments and buildings directly, but not the land under a house. The usual route for a house with a plot is a Bulgarian company, which can own land.

General information, not legal advice. Updated November 2026.

### What it costs to buy

About 3.2-8.5% on top of the price. On a €150,000 home that is €4,800 to €12,750, so €154,800 to €162,750 in total.

Transfer tax 0.1-3% (municipal; Sofia 2.5%) + notary 0.1-1.5% + legal 0.5-1% + agent 2.5-3%.

[Work it out for your price](https://realhunt.co/buying-costs/bulgaria)

### Every year

Yearly property tax: 0.01-0.45% of the property's tax value plus a municipal garbage fee.

Yearly costs are low: municipal property tax is 0.01% to 0.45% of the tax assessment value, with a 5% discount if paid in full by April 30, plus a municipal waste collection fee. Owning through a company adds about EUR 500 to 1,500 a year in running costs.

Tax on rental income: Non-residents: 10% final tax on gross rent, paid quarterly, no deductions.

### Living there

Buying a home gives no right to live in Bulgaria; longer stays need a residence permit.

Bulgaria is in the Schengen area: with an American passport you can usually stay up to 90 days in any 180 days across the whole area without a visa.

### Good to know as an American

- The US taxes its citizens on worldwide income, so rent from a home abroad goes on your US return, and foreign bank accounts above US$10,000 in total need an FBAR report.
- Some banks abroad are slow to open accounts for US citizens because of FATCA reporting, so ask early.

### The steps to buy in Bulgaria

- Check what you can own
- Hire a lawyer and check the property
- Sign a preliminary contract
- Get your documents ready
- Sign the deed before a notary
- Declare the property to the municipality

[The full guide, step by step](https://realhunt.co/guide/bulgaria)

## Can an American buy property in Canada?

Short answer: Restricted.

Mostly not for now: a federal ban stops non-Canadians from buying homes in cities and larger towns until 1 January 2027. It does not cover rural areas and small towns, and there are exceptions, such as some work permit holders. Check the current status before you look: the government has said a replacement is being studied.

General information, not legal advice. Updated November 2026.

### What it costs to buy

About 1.5-4% on top of the price. On a €150,000 home that is €2,250 to €6,000, so €152,250 to €156,000 in total.

Buyers usually pay provincial land transfer tax on a sliding scale (Ontario: 0.5% up to $55,000 and 1% from $55,000 to $250,000), legal fees of about $500 to $1,500, title insurance of about $250 and an inspection of $300 to $1,000, while the seller usually pays the agents; foreign buyers also pay Ontario's 25% non-resident speculation tax anywhere in Ontario and British Columbia's 20% additional tax in Metro Vancouver and four other regions.

[Work it out for your price](https://realhunt.co/buying-costs/canada)

### Every year

Yearly property tax: Property tax is set by each city as a share of assessed value, from about 0.3% in Vancouver to 2.12% in Saint John in 2026.

Expect municipal property tax, from about 0.3% to 2.1% of assessed value depending on the city, plus insurance and upkeep. The federal Underused Housing Tax is proposed to end from 2025, but the change was still in Bill C-15 when last checked.

Tax on rental income: Non-residents have 25% of gross rent withheld, but they can file a Section 216 return to pay tax on net rent instead, and Form NR6 lets the agent withhold on net rent.

### Living there

Buying a home gives no right to live in Canada.

### Good to know as an American

- The US taxes its citizens on worldwide income, so rent from a home abroad goes on your US return, and foreign bank accounts above US$10,000 in total need an FBAR report.
- Some banks abroad are slow to open accounts for US citizens because of FATCA reporting, so ask early.

### The steps to buy in Canada

- Check if you can buy
- Check provincial foreign buyer taxes
- Hire a real estate lawyer
- Make an offer
- Close the sale
- Arrange rental tax filings

[The full guide, step by step](https://realhunt.co/guide/canada)

## Can an American buy property in Cyprus?

Short answer: Yes, with conditions.

Yes, with a permit: Americans need permission from the Council of Ministers, applied for through the District Officer, and are normally limited to one home or a plot of up to 4,014 m². The permit is a formality for most buyers, but it takes time.

General information, not legal advice. Updated November 2026.

### What it costs to buy

About 2.5-3.5% on top of the price. On a €150,000 home that is €3,750 to €5,250, so €153,750 to €155,250 in total.

Land Registry transfer fees of 3% up to €85,000, 5% to €170,000 and 8% above, halved for resales without VAT (1.5%, 2.5% and 4%); stamp duty abolished from 1 January 2026; lawyer about 1% plus VAT; small Land Registry charges.

[Work it out for your price](https://realhunt.co/buying-costs/cyprus)

### Every year

Yearly property tax: There is no annual national property tax (abolished in 2017); owners pay municipal fees of about €90 to €300 a year, plus sewerage and local authority charges.

Yearly costs are municipal, sewerage and local authority fees, plus income tax and GHS on any rent.

Tax on rental income: Non-residents pay income tax on Cyprus rental income at 20% to 35% after deducting 20% of the gross rent and loan interest, plus a 2.65% health contribution (GHS); the special defence contribution does not apply to them.

### Living there

Non-EU buyers of a new home worth at least €300,000 plus VAT can apply for permanent residency under the Cyprus investment route; the conditions were tightened in 2023, so check the current rules.

### Good to know as an American

- The US taxes its citizens on worldwide income, so rent from a home abroad goes on your US return, and foreign bank accounts above US$10,000 in total need an FBAR report.
- Some banks abroad are slow to open accounts for US citizens because of FATCA reporting, so ask early.

### The steps to buy in Cyprus

- Hire a lawyer
- Check the title
- Sign the contract
- Lodge the contract
- Apply for permission if non-EU
- Transfer the title

## Can an American buy property in Denmark?

Short answer: Restricted.

Restricted. Without Danish residence (or 5 years of past residence) Americans need permission from the Department of Civil Affairs (Civilstyrelsen), which is rarely given just to buy a home. Holiday homes (sommerhuse) are only allowed for people with strong, long ties to Denmark.

General information, not legal advice. Updated November 2026.

### What it costs to buy

About 1.5-3% on top of the price. On a €150,000 home that is €2,250 to €4,500, so €152,250 to €154,500 in total.

Registration fee on the deed (tinglysningsafgift) of DKK 1,850 plus 0.6% of the price, about 1% for a buyer's lawyer, and, if you borrow, a mortgage registration fee of DKK 1,825 plus 1.25% of the loan; the seller normally pays the agent.

[Work it out for your price](https://realhunt.co/buying-costs/denmark)

### Every year

Yearly property tax: Owners pay property value tax (ejendomsværdiskat) of 0.51% on 80% of the official valuation (1.4% above DKK 9.2 million) plus municipal land tax (grundskyld) at a rate set by each municipality, capped at 30 per mille of the land value.

Expect property value tax and municipal land tax, both charged through the Danish tax system, plus insurance, utilities and upkeep. Owners abroad may need to file a Danish tax return if they rent the home out.

Tax on rental income: A non-resident who rents out a Danish home is taxed in Denmark on the profit under the ordinary Danish rules; staying in Denmark more than 3 months at a time or 180 days a year, or working there, makes you fully tax liable.

### Living there

Buying a home gives no right to live in Denmark.

Denmark is in the Schengen area: with an American passport you can usually stay up to 90 days in any 180 days across the whole area without a visa.

### Good to know as an American

- The US taxes its citizens on worldwide income, so rent from a home abroad goes on your US return, and foreign bank accounts above US$10,000 in total need an FBAR report.
- Some banks abroad are slow to open accounts for US citizens because of FATCA reporting, so ask early.

### The steps to buy in Denmark

- Check if you need permission
- Get a Danish tax number
- Set a budget with a bank
- Make an offer and sign with conditions
- Let your lawyer check the documents
- Register the deed

[The full guide, step by step](https://realhunt.co/guide/denmark)

## Can an American buy property in the Dominican Republic?

Short answer: Yes.

Yes. Americans have the same rights as Dominican citizens to buy land and homes, with no restrictions.

General information, not legal advice. Updated November 2026.

### What it costs to buy

About 4.25-7% on top of the price. On a €150,000 home that is €6,375 to €10,500, so €156,375 to €160,500 in total.

The buyer pays a 3% transfer tax (0% for qualifying first purchases under CONFOTUR tourism incentives), legal fees of about 1-2% and notary fees of about 0.25-1%, plus registration costs, while the seller pays the 2-3% agent fee.

[Work it out for your price](https://realhunt.co/buying-costs/dominican-republic)

### Every year

Yearly property tax: The yearly IPI tax is 1% of the part of a person's total Dominican property value, as assessed by the tax office DGII, above RD$10,695,494 in 2026, so a single cheap home is often below the threshold.

Most single homes under about $150,000 pay no IPI property tax because they fall under the threshold, but expect condo fees, utilities and upkeep. A 2026 tax law (Law 30-26) sets a 10% tax on gains when an individual sells, though its regulations were still in draft in October 2026.

Tax on rental income: Rent paid abroad to a non-resident is generally subject to 27% withholding.

### Living there

Buying a home does not by itself give you residency in the Dominican Republic.

### Good to know as an American

- The US taxes its citizens on worldwide income, so rent from a home abroad goes on your US return, and foreign bank accounts above US$10,000 in total need an FBAR report.
- Some banks abroad are slow to open accounts for US citizens because of FATCA reporting, so ask early.

### The steps to buy in the Dominican Republic

- Get a tax ID (RNC)
- Check the title
- Sign a promise of sale
- Sign the deed before a notary
- Pay the transfer tax
- Register the title

[The full guide, step by step](https://realhunt.co/guide/dominican-republic)

## Can an American buy property in France?

Short answer: Yes.

Yes. Americans can buy property in France without restrictions and need no permit.

General information, not legal advice. Updated November 2026.

### What it costs to buy

About 7-8.5% on top of the price. On a €150,000 home that is €10,500 to €12,750, so €160,500 to €162,750 in total.

Transfer taxes (droits de mutation) of about 5.8%, or about 6.3% in departments that raised their rate for 2025 to March 2028; notary fee (émoluments) on a sliding scale from 3.87% down to 0.799% plus 20% VAT, about 1.3% on a €150,000 home; land security contribution (contribution de sécurité immobilière) 0.10%; disbursements (débours) of about €800 to €1,200; the agent fee is usually built into the advertised price (FAI) and paid by the seller, sometimes shared.

[Work it out for your price](https://realhunt.co/buying-costs/france)

### Every year

Yearly property tax: Owners pay an annual property tax (taxe foncière) set by the local authorities, and owners of a furnished second home also pay housing tax (taxe d'habitation), which some communes raise by a surcharge of 5% to 60%.

Expect the annual taxe foncière, plus taxe d'habitation if the home is a furnished second home, and income tax and social charges on any rent.

Tax on rental income: Non-residents pay French income tax on French rental income at a minimum rate of 20% (30% above about €27,500), plus social charges of 17.2%, or 7.5% for people covered by social security in another EU/EEA country or Switzerland.

### Living there

Buying a home gives no right to live in France; stays over 90 days need a long-stay visa.

France is in the Schengen area: with an American passport you can usually stay up to 90 days in any 180 days across the whole area without a visa.

### Good to know as an American

- The US taxes its citizens on worldwide income, so rent from a home abroad goes on your US return, and foreign bank accounts above US$10,000 in total need an FBAR report.
- Some banks abroad are slow to open accounts for US citizens because of FATCA reporting, so ask early.

### The steps to buy in France

- Make an offer
- Sign the preliminary contract
- Use the cooling-off period
- Pay the deposit
- Let the notary run checks
- Sign the final deed

## Can an American buy property in Germany?

General information, not legal advice. Updated November 2026.

### What it costs to buy

About 5-8.5% on top of the price. On a €150,000 home that is €7,500 to €12,750, so €157,500 to €162,750 in total.

Real estate transfer tax (Grunderwerbsteuer) of 3.5% to 6.5% depending on the state (3.5% in Bavaria, 6.5% in Brandenburg, North Rhine-Westphalia, Saarland and Schleswig-Holstein), plus notary and land registry fees (Notar- und Grundbuchkosten) of about 1.5-2%; if the seller hired the agent, the buyer pays half the commission by law, which is extra.

[Work it out for your price](https://realhunt.co/buying-costs/germany)

### Every year

Yearly property tax: Owners pay property tax (Grundsteuer), calculated since 2025 as assessed value x a tax rate x a municipal multiplier (Hebesatz) that each municipality sets.

Expect the municipal property tax, insurance, utilities and upkeep. Rental profit is taxable in Germany, so a non-resident landlord deals with a German tax office.

Tax on rental income: Non-resident owners are taxed in Germany on net rental income at the normal progressive income tax rates, but without the basic tax-free allowance (Grundfreibetrag).

### Living there

Buying a home gives no right to live in Germany.

Germany is in the Schengen area: with an American passport you can usually stay up to 90 days in any 180 days across the whole area without a visa.

### Good to know as an American

- The US taxes its citizens on worldwide income, so rent from a home abroad goes on your US return, and foreign bank accounts above US$10,000 in total need an FBAR report.
- Some banks abroad are slow to open accounts for US citizens because of FATCA reporting, so ask early.

### The steps to buy in Germany

- Find a home and arrange money
- Get independent advice
- Sign before a notary
- Secure a priority notice
- Pay the transfer tax and the price
- Get registered as owner

## Can an American buy property in Greece?

Short answer: Yes, with conditions.

Yes, with one condition: Americans need a permit to buy in designated border areas (parts of northern Greece and eastern Aegean islands such as Rhodes and the Dodecanese). Elsewhere you buy like a Greek. The government has also announced a 15% transfer tax for non-EU buyers from 1 January 2027, not yet final.

General information, not legal advice. Updated November 2026.

### What it costs to buy

About 5.5-7% on top of the price. On a €150,000 home that is €8,250 to €10,500, so €158,250 to €160,500 in total.

Transfer tax 3.09% of the price or the taxable value, whichever is higher; notary about 0.8-1% plus VAT; land registry fees about 0.5-0.7%; lawyer 1-2% plus VAT; if an agent is used, the buyer usually pays a commission of 1-3% plus VAT on top.

[Work it out for your price](https://realhunt.co/buying-costs/greece)

### Every year

Yearly property tax: Owners on 1 January pay the unified property tax (ENFIA), calculated per property from its location, size, age and official zone value, with an extra charge if total Greek property exceeds €500,000.

Yearly costs are ENFIA and income tax on any rent.

Tax on rental income: Non-residents pay Greek tax on Greek rental income at 15% up to €12,000, 25% to €24,000, 35% to €36,000 and 45% above, after a flat 5% deduction for expenses.

### Living there

Greece has a golden visa for non-EU buyers. Since 2024 the minimum is €800,000 in Attica, Thessaloniki, Mykonos, Santorini and larger islands, and €400,000 elsewhere, so a cheap home does not qualify.

Greece is in the Schengen area: with an American passport you can usually stay up to 90 days in any 180 days across the whole area without a visa.

### Good to know as an American

- The US taxes its citizens on worldwide income, so rent from a home abroad goes on your US return, and foreign bank accounts above US$10,000 in total need an FBAR report.
- Some banks abroad are slow to open accounts for US citizens because of FATCA reporting, so ask early.

### The steps to buy in Greece

- Get a Greek tax number
- Hire a lawyer
- Check the title
- Sign a private agreement
- Pay the transfer tax
- Sign the deed and register it

[The full guide, step by step](https://realhunt.co/guide/greece)

## Can an American buy property in Italy?

Short answer: Yes.

Yes. Italy lets non-EU citizens buy when their country lets Italians buy (reciprocity), and the US, UK, Canada, Australia and Switzerland all qualify. You need an Italian tax code (codice fiscale).

General information, not legal advice. Updated November 2026.

### What it costs to buy

About 4-15% on top of the price. On a €150,000 home that is €6,000 to €22,500, so €156,000 to €172,500 in total.

Registration tax 9% on a second home (resale), or VAT on new builds; notary 1-2% + legal ~1% + agent ~3% (GPG roundtrip 10-18%).

[Work it out for your price](https://realhunt.co/buying-costs/italy)

### Every year

Yearly property tax: IMU 0.4-1.06% on second homes (on cadastral value).

IMU (council property tax) on second homes and a local waste tax (TARI). For small rural houses these are often a few hundred euros a year.

Tax on rental income: Optional flat 'cedolare secca' on short lets: 21% for one property, 26% from the second.

### Living there

Buying a home gives no right to live in Italy; stays over 90 days need a visa, such as the elective residence visa.

Italy is in the Schengen area: with an American passport you can usually stay up to 90 days in any 180 days across the whole area without a visa.

### Good to know as an American

- The US taxes its citizens on worldwide income, so rent from a home abroad goes on your US return, and foreign bank accounts above US$10,000 in total need an FBAR report.
- Some banks abroad are slow to open accounts for US citizens because of FATCA reporting, so ask early.

### The steps to buy in Italy

- Get a codice fiscale
- Make a written offer
- Check the house
- Sign at the notary
- Pay the taxes

[The full guide, step by step](https://realhunt.co/guide/italy)

## Can an American buy property in Japan?

Short answer: Yes.

Yes. Americans can buy freehold land and homes on the same terms as Japanese citizens, even on a tourist visa.

General information, not legal advice. Updated November 2026.

### What it costs to buy

About 6-9% on top of the price. On a €150,000 home that is €9,000 to €13,500, so €159,000 to €163,500 in total.

The buyer pays an agent fee capped at 3% plus ¥60,000 plus 10% consumption tax (with a special cap of up to ¥330,000 including tax for cheap vacant homes up to ¥8 million), registration tax of 1.5% on land (until March 2029) and 2% standard on the building, real estate acquisition tax of 3% of assessed value, stamp duty, and a judicial scrivener fee of about ¥100,000 to ¥200,000.

[Work it out for your price](https://realhunt.co/buying-costs/japan)

### Every year

Yearly property tax: Fixed asset tax is 1.4% of the government's assessed value, plus city planning tax of up to 0.3% in urban areas, and small residential plots get a lower tax base.

Expect fixed asset tax of 1.4% and city planning tax of up to 0.3% of assessed value, which is usually well below market value. Add the cost of a tax representative and, for apartments, monthly management and repair fund fees.

Tax on rental income: Rent paid to a non-resident is subject to 20.42% withholding (except when an individual rents it as their own home), and the owner must file a tax return each year through a tax representative in Japan to settle the final tax.

### Living there

Buying a home gives no visa or residency in Japan.

### Good to know as an American

- The US taxes its citizens on worldwide income, so rent from a home abroad goes on your US return, and foreign bank accounts above US$10,000 in total need an FBAR report.
- Some banks abroad are slow to open accounts for US citizens because of FATCA reporting, so ask early.

### The steps to buy in Japan

- Find a home and agent
- Submit a written offer
- Hear the property explanation
- Sign and pay a deposit
- Pay and register
- File reports and name a tax representative

[The full guide, step by step](https://realhunt.co/guide/japan)

### Questions

#### Can an American buy property in Japan?

Yes. Americans can buy freehold land and homes on the same terms as Japanese citizens, even on a tourist visa.

#### How much are the buying costs in Japan?

About 6-9% on top of the price, so €9,000 to €13,500 on a €150,000 home. The buyer pays an agent fee capped at 3% plus ¥60,000 plus 10% consumption tax (with a special cap of up to ¥330,000 including tax for cheap vacant homes up to ¥8 million), registration tax of 1.5% on land (until March 2029) and 2% standard on the building, real estate acquisition tax of 3% of assessed value, stamp duty, and a judicial scrivener fee of about ¥100,000 to ¥200,000.

#### Is there a yearly property tax in Japan?

Fixed asset tax is 1.4% of the government's assessed value, plus city planning tax of up to 0.3% in urban areas, and small residential plots get a lower tax base.

#### What tax do I pay on rent in Japan if I live abroad?

Rent paid to a non-resident is subject to 20.42% withholding (except when an individual rents it as their own home), and the owner must file a tax return each year through a tax representative in Japan to settle the final tax.

#### Does buying a home in Japan let me live there as an American?

Buying a home gives no visa or residency in Japan.

## Can an American buy property in Mexico?

Short answer: Yes, with conditions.

Yes, with conditions. In the Restricted Zone (within 50 km of the coast or 100 km of the borders, which covers Tulum and Playa del Carmen) Americans buy through a fideicomiso bank trust or a Mexican company. Inland you can own directly, with a permit from the Foreign Ministry.

General information, not legal advice. Updated November 2026.

### What it costs to buy

About 3.5-8% on top of the price. On a €150,000 home that is €5,250 to €12,000, so €155,250 to €162,000 in total.

Acquisition tax 2-5% + notary 0.5-1% + legal 1-1.5% (GPG 3.5-7.5%), plus 0.5-1.5% for fideicomiso/permit setup; TheLatinvestor budgets 5-8%.

[Work it out for your price](https://realhunt.co/buying-costs/mexico)

### Every year

Yearly property tax: Municipal predial, set locally on cadastral value; usually small, often less than HOA fees.

Yearly costs include the local property tax (predial), usually 0.05% to 1.2% of the official cadastral value, which is often well below market value. In the restricted zone add the bank trust fee, about US$450 to US$1,000 a year, plus HOA fees, insurance and upkeep.

Tax on rental income: Non-residents: 25% ISR withholding on gross rent; plus 16% IVA on short-term stays (Airbnb remits on its bookings).

### Living there

Buying a home gives no residency in Mexico; temporary residency is usually based on income or savings and applied for at a Mexican consulate.

### Good to know as an American

- The US taxes its citizens on worldwide income, so rent from a home abroad goes on your US return, and foreign bank accounts above US$10,000 in total need an FBAR report.
- Some banks abroad are slow to open accounts for US citizens because of FATCA reporting, so ask early.

### The steps to buy in Mexico

- Check the restricted zone
- Choose how to hold title
- Check the title
- Sign the purchase contract
- Close with a notary
- Register the deed

[The full guide, step by step](https://realhunt.co/guide/mexico)

## Can an American buy property in the Netherlands?

Short answer: Yes.

Yes. There are no nationality or residence rules and no surcharge for foreign buyers in the Netherlands. Some cities restrict renting out cheaper homes after you buy (opkoopbescherming).

General information, not legal advice. Updated November 2026.

### What it costs to buy

About 2-9% on top of the price. On a €150,000 home that is €3,000 to €13,500, so €153,000 to €163,500 in total.

Transfer tax (overdrachtsbelasting) of 8% if you will not live in the home, such as a buy-to-let or holiday home, or 2% if it becomes your main home; a notary fee for the transfer deed of around EUR 500; Kadaster registration fees; and mortgage costs if you borrow; the seller pays its own agent.

[Work it out for your price](https://realhunt.co/buying-costs/netherlands)

### Every year

Yearly property tax: Owners pay municipal property tax (onroerendezaakbelasting, OZB) on the official WOZ value, at a rate each municipality sets, which in practice is a per mille figure; tenants of homes do not pay it.

Expect municipal property tax (OZB), insurance and upkeep, and in a flat the owners' association (VvE) contribution. Non-residents also pay box 3 income tax based on the property's value.

Tax on rental income: Non-residents declare Dutch property in box 3, where tax is 36% on a deemed return of 6% of the property's value in 2026, after a tax-free allowance of EUR 59,357 per person, regardless of actual rent.

### Living there

Buying a home gives no right to live in the Netherlands.

The Netherlands is in the Schengen area: with an American passport you can usually stay up to 90 days in any 180 days across the whole area without a visa.

### Good to know as an American

- The US taxes its citizens on worldwide income, so rent from a home abroad goes on your US return, and foreign bank accounts above US$10,000 in total need an FBAR report.
- Some banks abroad are slow to open accounts for US citizens because of FATCA reporting, so ask early.

### The steps to buy in the Netherlands

- Get a BSN
- Set up payment and money
- Make an offer
- Use the 3-day cooling-off period
- Pay the deposit
- Sign the deed and register

[The full guide, step by step](https://realhunt.co/guide/netherlands)

## Can an American buy property in Norway?

Short answer: Yes.

Yes. Anyone with the funds can buy property in Norway, and a built plot of up to 2 decares normally needs no concession (konsesjon). Farms and larger plots need a concession.

General information, not legal advice. Updated November 2026.

### What it costs to buy

About 2.5-3% on top of the price. On a €150,000 home that is €3,750 to €4,500, so €153,750 to €154,500 in total.

Document duty (dokumentavgift) of 2.5% of market value, a registration fee (tinglysingsgebyr) of NOK 545 for the deed and NOK 545 for any mortgage document; a flat in a housing cooperative (borettslag) has no document duty; the seller normally pays the agent.

[Work it out for your price](https://realhunt.co/buying-costs/norway)

### Every year

Yearly property tax: Some municipalities charge property tax (eiendomsskatt), at most 4 per mille of the value after a reduction of at least 30%, and some also give a basic deduction; many charge nothing.

Expect municipal property tax where it applies, municipal fees, insurance and upkeep. Costs such as municipal fees and property tax are deductible against rental income.

Tax on rental income: Rental profit is normally taxed at 22%, and the Tax Administration says its rental rules also apply to owners who are tax resident abroad.

### Living there

Buying a home gives no right to live in Norway.

Norway is in the Schengen area: with an American passport you can usually stay up to 90 days in any 180 days across the whole area without a visa.

### Good to know as an American

- The US taxes its citizens on worldwide income, so rent from a home abroad goes on your US return, and foreign bank accounts above US$10,000 in total need an FBAR report.
- Some banks abroad are slow to open accounts for US citizens because of FATCA reporting, so ask early.

### The steps to buy in Norway

- Find a home and get loan approval
- Bid through the agent
- Sign the contract
- Pay at settlement
- Get a D-number if needed
- Register the deed

[The full guide, step by step](https://realhunt.co/guide/norway)

## Can an American buy property in Poland?

Short answer: Yes, with conditions.

Partly: Americans can buy an apartment without a permit, but usually need a permit from the Ministry of the Interior (MSWiA) to buy a house or land.

General information, not legal advice. Updated November 2026.

### What it costs to buy

About 2.5-4% on top of the price. On a €150,000 home that is €3,750 to €6,000, so €153,750 to €156,000 in total.

Tax on civil law transactions (PCC) 2% of the value, paid by the buyer within 14 days of the deed; notary fee (taksa notarialna) capped at PLN 1,010 plus 0.4% of the value above PLN 60,000, plus 23% VAT; court fee of PLN 200 to enter ownership in the land register (plus PLN 100 for a new register); optional lawyer about 1%; the agent fee (about 2-3%) depends on the agreement.

[Work it out for your price](https://realhunt.co/buying-costs/poland)

### Every year

Yearly property tax: Owners pay a local property tax (podatek od nieruchomości) set by the commune, capped in 2026 at PLN 1.25 per m² of usable floor space for flats and houses.

Yearly costs are the local property tax, which is low for flats, plus income tax on any rent.

Tax on rental income: Private rental income is taxed as a flat lump sum (ryczałt) of 8.5% of revenue up to PLN 100,000 a year and 12.5% above that.

### Living there

Buying a home gives no right to live in Poland.

Poland is in the Schengen area: with an American passport you can usually stay up to 90 days in any 180 days across the whole area without a visa.

### Good to know as an American

- The US taxes its citizens on worldwide income, so rent from a home abroad goes on your US return, and foreign bank accounts above US$10,000 in total need an FBAR report.
- Some banks abroad are slow to open accounts for US citizens because of FATCA reporting, so ask early.

### The steps to buy in Poland

- Get a PESEL number
- Check if you need a permit
- Sign a preliminary agreement
- Do due diligence
- Sign the notarial deed
- Pay the PCC tax

[The full guide, step by step](https://realhunt.co/guide/poland)

## Can an American buy property in Portugal?

Short answer: Yes.

Yes. Americans buy in Portugal with the same rights as Portuguese citizens. You need a Portuguese tax number (NIF).

General information, not legal advice. Updated November 2026.

### What it costs to buy

About 3-12% on top of the price. On a €150,000 home that is €4,500 to €18,000, so €154,500 to €168,000 in total.

IMT transfer tax 0-8% (progressive) + stamp duty 0.8% + notary/registry 0.9-1.2% + legal 1.25-2%.

[Work it out for your price](https://realhunt.co/buying-costs/portugal)

### Every year

Yearly property tax: IMI 0.3-0.45% of taxable value (urban), set by municipality.

IMI (council tax), usually 0.3–0.45% of the tax value for urban property.

Tax on rental income: Long-term: 25% flat for non-residents; short-term (AL) under the simplified regime only 35-50% of gross is taxable.

### Living there

Since October 2023, buying a home no longer qualifies for Portugal's golden visa. The D7 visa for people with passive income is the usual route to live there.

Portugal is in the Schengen area: with an American passport you can usually stay up to 90 days in any 180 days across the whole area without a visa.

### Good to know as an American

- The US taxes its citizens on worldwide income, so rent from a home abroad goes on your US return, and foreign bank accounts above US$10,000 in total need an FBAR report.
- Some banks abroad are slow to open accounts for US citizens because of FATCA reporting, so ask early.

### The steps to buy in Portugal

- Sign a promissory contract
- Check the house
- Sign the deed
- Pay the taxes
