## Can an American buy property in Spain?

Short answer: Yes.

Yes, for now. Americans buy in Spain on the same terms as Spaniards and need an NIE, the foreigner tax number. The government has proposed a 100% tax on (or a ban for) non-EU buyers who do not live in Spain; it is not law as of November 2026, so check before you sign.

General information, not legal advice. Updated November 2026.

### What it costs to buy

About 7.5-14% on top of the price. On a €150,000 home that is €11,250 to €21,000, so €161,250 to €171,000 in total.

New build: 10% IVA + 0.5-1.5% AJD stamp duty + notary 0.5-1% + legal 1-2%; resale: ITP transfer tax 6-11% instead of IVA/AJD.

[Work it out for your price](https://realhunt.co/buying-costs/spain)

### Every year

Yearly property tax: IBI 0.4-1.1% of cadastral value (municipal), plus imputed income tax on unlet homes.

IBI (council tax) and waste collection. Non-residents who do not rent the house out also file a small yearly imputed-income tax.

Tax on rental income: Non-residents: EU/EEA 19% on net income; non-EU 24% on gross with no deductions.

### Living there

Buying a home gives no right to live in Spain: the golden visa for property buyers closed on 3 April 2025. The non-lucrative visa is the usual route for people with passive income.

Spain is in the Schengen area: with an American passport you can usually stay up to 90 days in any 180 days across the whole area without a visa.

### Good to know as an American

- The US taxes its citizens on worldwide income, so rent from a home abroad goes on your US return, and foreign bank accounts above US$10,000 in total need an FBAR report.
- Some banks abroad are slow to open accounts for US citizens because of FATCA reporting, so ask early.

### The steps to buy in Spain

- Get an NIE
- Open a Spanish bank account
- Reserve with an arras contract
- Check the house
- Sign at the notary and register
- Pay the transfer tax

[The full guide, step by step](https://realhunt.co/guide/spain)

## Can an American buy property in Sweden?

Short answer: Yes.

Yes. There are no citizenship or residence rules for buying a home in Sweden. You need a Swedish personal identity number or a coordination number (samordningsnummer) to register ownership.

General information, not legal advice. Updated November 2026.

### What it costs to buy

About 1.5-3.5% on top of the price. On a €150,000 home that is €2,250 to €5,250, so €152,250 to €155,250 in total.

Stamp duty on the title (lagfart) of 1.5% of the price or tax value, whichever is higher, plus a SEK 825 fee; if you borrow and need new mortgage deeds (pantbrev), 2% of their amount plus a SEK 375 fee; optional legal advice; the seller normally pays the agent, and a cooperative flat (bostadsrätt) has no lagfart.

[Work it out for your price](https://realhunt.co/buying-costs/sweden)

### Every year

Yearly property tax: Houses pay a municipal property fee (kommunal fastighetsavgift) of SEK 10,425 in 2026, or 0.75% of the tax value if that is lower.

House owners pay the municipal property fee and must file a Swedish tax return if they owe it or have rental income, even when living abroad. Add insurance, utilities and upkeep.

Tax on rental income: Non-resident individuals pay 30% tax on net rental income as capital income; for a private home you can first deduct SEK 40,000 per property and 20% of the rent (the 20% does not apply to a bostadsrätt).

### Living there

Buying a home gives no right to live in Sweden.

Sweden is in the Schengen area: with an American passport you can usually stay up to 90 days in any 180 days across the whole area without a visa.

### Good to know as an American

- The US taxes its citizens on worldwide income, so rent from a home abroad goes on your US return, and foreign bank accounts above US$10,000 in total need an FBAR report.

### Questions

#### Can an American buy property in Sweden?

Yes. There are no citizenship or residence rules for buying a home in Sweden. You need a Swedish personal identity number or a coordination number (samordningsnummer) to register ownership.

#### How much are the buying costs in Sweden?

About 1.5-3.5% on top of the price, so €2,250 to €5,250 on a €150,000 home. Stamp duty on the title (lagfart) of 1.5% of the price or tax value, whichever is higher, plus a SEK 825 fee; if you borrow and need new mortgage deeds (pantbrev), 2% of their amount plus a SEK 375 fee; optional legal advice; the seller normally pays the agent, and a cooperative flat (bostadsrätt) has no lagfart.

#### Is there a yearly property tax in Sweden?

Houses pay a municipal property fee (kommunal fastighetsavgift) of SEK 10,425 in 2026, or 0.75% of the tax value if that is lower.

#### What tax do I pay on rent in Sweden if I live abroad?

Non-resident individuals pay 30% tax on net rental income as capital income; for a private home you can first deduct SEK 40,000 per property and 20% of the rent (the 20% does not apply to a bostadsrätt).

#### Does buying a home in Sweden let me live there as an American?

Buying a home gives no right to live in Sweden. Sweden is in the Schengen area: with an American passport you can usually stay up to 90 days in any 180 days across the whole area without a visa.

## Can an American buy property in Switzerland?

Short answer: Restricted.

Restricted. Under the Lex Koller law, Americans living abroad need a cantonal permit and can usually only buy one holiday home in a tourist area, within national quotas. Living in Switzerland, holders of a C permit buy like Swiss citizens, and holders of a B permit can buy the home they live in.

General information, not legal advice. Updated November 2026.

### What it costs to buy

About 1-5% on top of the price. On a €150,000 home that is €1,500 to €7,500, so €151,500 to €157,500 in total.

Transfer tax (Handänderungssteuer, droits de mutation) 0% to about 3.3% depending on the canton; notary about 0.1-0.5%; land register fee, a small fixed amount or percentage; optional lawyer 1-2%; the agent fee (2-3%) is paid by the seller.

[Work it out for your price](https://realhunt.co/buying-costs/switzerland)

### Every year

Yearly property tax: More than half of the cantons charge an annual property tax (Liegenschaftssteuer), usually 0.01-0.3% of the assessed value, and owners also pay cantonal wealth tax on the property value minus the mortgage.

Yearly costs are wealth tax, cantonal property tax where it exists, and tax on imputed rental value (Eigenmietwert) if you use the home yourself. Imputed rental value is due to end on 1 January 2029, and cantons may then add a new tax on second homes.

Tax on rental income: Non-residents pay tax on net Swiss rental income at ordinary cantonal and communal rates plus federal direct tax, and some cantons set the rate using worldwide income.

### Living there

Buying a home gives no right to live in Switzerland.

Switzerland is in the Schengen area: with an American passport you can usually stay up to 90 days in any 180 days across the whole area without a visa.

### Good to know as an American

- The US taxes its citizens on worldwide income, so rent from a home abroad goes on your US return, and foreign bank accounts above US$10,000 in total need an FBAR report.
- Some banks abroad are slow to open accounts for US citizens because of FATCA reporting, so ask early.

### The steps to buy in Switzerland

- Check your Lex Koller status
- Arrange financing
- Find a property and make an offer
- Sign the deed at a notary
- Register the transfer

## Can an American buy property in the United Kingdom?

Short answer: Yes.

Yes. There are no nationality restrictions on buying homes anywhere in the UK. In England and Northern Ireland, buyers who do not live in the UK pay a 2% stamp duty surcharge.

General information, not legal advice. Updated November 2026.

### What it costs to buy

About 3-9% on top of the price. On a €150,000 home that is €4,500 to €13,500, so €154,500 to €163,500 in total.

In England and Northern Ireland, Stamp Duty Land Tax (SDLT) is 0% up to £125,000 and 2% from £125,001 to £250,000, plus a 2% surcharge for non-UK residents and a further 5% if you already own a home anywhere, so a non-resident who owns another home pays 7% up to £125,000 and 9% to £250,000; solicitor (conveyancer) about 0.6-1% with a typical minimum of around £2,100 including VAT; Land Registry fee £20 to £230; searches extra; the seller pays the estate agent.

[Work it out for your price](https://realhunt.co/buying-costs/united-kingdom)

### Every year

Yearly property tax: Owners or occupiers pay council tax to the local council, and many councils in England charge second homes a premium of up to 100% from April 2025.

Yearly costs are council tax, which may include a second home premium, plus a self assessment tax return and income tax if you let the home.

Tax on rental income: Non-resident landlords pay UK income tax on rent at 20%, 40% or 45%, with 20% deducted at source by the agent or tenant unless HMRC approves gross payment, and the rates on property income are set to rise to 22%, 42% and 47% from April 2027.

### Living there

Buying a home gives no right to live in the UK. Visitors can usually stay up to 6 months, and most now need an electronic travel authorisation (ETA) before they travel.

### Good to know as an American

- The US taxes its citizens on worldwide income, so rent from a home abroad goes on your US return, and foreign bank accounts above US$10,000 in total need an FBAR report.
- Some banks abroad are slow to open accounts for US citizens because of FATCA reporting, so ask early.

- Instruct a solicitor
- Run searches and enquiries
- Exchange contracts
- Complete
- Pay SDLT and register

## Can an Australian buy property in Bulgaria?

Short answer: Yes, with conditions.

Yes, with a condition: Australians can own apartments and buildings directly, but not the land under a house. The usual route for a house with a plot is a Bulgarian company, which can own land.

General information, not legal advice. Updated November 2026.

### What it costs to buy

About 3.2-8.5% on top of the price. On a €150,000 home that is €4,800 to €12,750, so €154,800 to €162,750 in total.

Transfer tax 0.1-3% (municipal; Sofia 2.5%) + notary 0.1-1.5% + legal 0.5-1% + agent 2.5-3%.

[Work it out for your price](https://realhunt.co/buying-costs/bulgaria)

### Every year

Yearly property tax: 0.01-0.45% of the property's tax value plus a municipal garbage fee.

Yearly costs are low: municipal property tax is 0.01% to 0.45% of the tax assessment value, with a 5% discount if paid in full by April 30, plus a municipal waste collection fee. Owning through a company adds about EUR 500 to 1,500 a year in running costs.

Tax on rental income: Non-residents: 10% final tax on gross rent, paid quarterly, no deductions.

### Living there

Buying a home gives no right to live in Bulgaria; longer stays need a residence permit.

Bulgaria is in the Schengen area: with an Australian passport you can usually stay up to 90 days in any 180 days across the whole area without a visa.

### Good to know as an Australian

## Can an Australian buy property in Canada?

Short answer: Restricted.

Mostly not for now: a federal ban stops non-Canadians from buying homes in cities and larger towns until 1 January 2027. It does not cover rural areas and small towns, and there are exceptions, such as some work permit holders. Check the current status before you look: the government has said a replacement is being studied.

General information, not legal advice. Updated November 2026.

### What it costs to buy

About 1.5-4% on top of the price. On a €150,000 home that is €2,250 to €6,000, so €152,250 to €156,000 in total.

Buyers usually pay provincial land transfer tax on a sliding scale (Ontario: 0.5% up to $55,000 and 1% from $55,000 to $250,000), legal fees of about $500 to $1,500, title insurance of about $250 and an inspection of $300 to $1,000, while the seller usually pays the agents; foreign buyers also pay Ontario's 25% non-resident speculation tax anywhere in Ontario and British Columbia's 20% additional tax in Metro Vancouver and four other regions.

[Work it out for your price](https://realhunt.co/buying-costs/canada)

### Every year

Yearly property tax: Property tax is set by each city as a share of assessed value, from about 0.3% in Vancouver to 2.12% in Saint John in 2026.

Expect municipal property tax, from about 0.3% to 2.1% of assessed value depending on the city, plus insurance and upkeep. The federal Underused Housing Tax is proposed to end from 2025, but the change was still in Bill C-15 when last checked.

Tax on rental income: Non-residents have 25% of gross rent withheld, but they can file a Section 216 return to pay tax on net rent instead, and Form NR6 lets the agent withhold on net rent.

### Living there

Buying a home gives no right to live in Canada.

### Good to know as an Australian

- Australian tax residents are taxed on worldwide income, so rent from a home abroad goes on your Australian return, usually with a credit for tax paid abroad.

- Check if you can buy
- Check provincial foreign buyer taxes
- Hire a real estate lawyer
- Make an offer
- Close the sale
- Arrange rental tax filings

## Can an Australian buy property in Cyprus?

Short answer: Yes, with conditions.

Yes, with a permit: Australians need permission from the Council of Ministers, applied for through the District Officer, and are normally limited to one home or a plot of up to 4,014 m². The permit is a formality for most buyers, but it takes time.

General information, not legal advice. Updated November 2026.

### What it costs to buy

About 2.5-3.5% on top of the price. On a €150,000 home that is €3,750 to €5,250, so €153,750 to €155,250 in total.

Land Registry transfer fees of 3% up to €85,000, 5% to €170,000 and 8% above, halved for resales without VAT (1.5%, 2.5% and 4%); stamp duty abolished from 1 January 2026; lawyer about 1% plus VAT; small Land Registry charges.

[Work it out for your price](https://realhunt.co/buying-costs/cyprus)

### Every year

Yearly property tax: There is no annual national property tax (abolished in 2017); owners pay municipal fees of about €90 to €300 a year, plus sewerage and local authority charges.

Yearly costs are municipal, sewerage and local authority fees, plus income tax and GHS on any rent.

Tax on rental income: Non-residents pay income tax on Cyprus rental income at 20% to 35% after deducting 20% of the gross rent and loan interest, plus a 2.65% health contribution (GHS); the special defence contribution does not apply to them.

### Living there

Non-EU buyers of a new home worth at least €300,000 plus VAT can apply for permanent residency under the Cyprus investment route; the conditions were tightened in 2023, so check the current rules.

### Good to know as an Australian

- Australian tax residents are taxed on worldwide income, so rent from a home abroad goes on your Australian return, usually with a credit for tax paid abroad.

### The steps to buy in Cyprus

- Hire a lawyer
- Check the title
- Sign the contract
- Lodge the contract
- Apply for permission if non-EU
- Transfer the title

[The full guide, step by step](https://realhunt.co/guide/cyprus)

## Can an Australian buy property in Denmark?

Short answer: Restricted.

Restricted. Without Danish residence (or 5 years of past residence) Australians need permission from the Department of Civil Affairs (Civilstyrelsen), which is rarely given just to buy a home. Holiday homes (sommerhuse) are only allowed for people with strong, long ties to Denmark.

General information, not legal advice. Updated November 2026.

### What it costs to buy

About 1.5-3% on top of the price. On a €150,000 home that is €2,250 to €4,500, so €152,250 to €154,500 in total.

Registration fee on the deed (tinglysningsafgift) of DKK 1,850 plus 0.6% of the price, about 1% for a buyer's lawyer, and, if you borrow, a mortgage registration fee of DKK 1,825 plus 1.25% of the loan; the seller normally pays the agent.

[Work it out for your price](https://realhunt.co/buying-costs/denmark)

### Every year

Yearly property tax: Owners pay property value tax (ejendomsværdiskat) of 0.51% on 80% of the official valuation (1.4% above DKK 9.2 million) plus municipal land tax (grundskyld) at a rate set by each municipality, capped at 30 per mille of the land value.

Expect property value tax and municipal land tax, both charged through the Danish tax system, plus insurance, utilities and upkeep. Owners abroad may need to file a Danish tax return if they rent the home out.

Tax on rental income: A non-resident who rents out a Danish home is taxed in Denmark on the profit under the ordinary Danish rules; staying in Denmark more than 3 months at a time or 180 days a year, or working there, makes you fully tax liable.

### Living there

Buying a home gives no right to live in Denmark.

Denmark is in the Schengen area: with an Australian passport you can usually stay up to 90 days in any 180 days across the whole area without a visa.

### Good to know as an Australian

- Australian tax residents are taxed on worldwide income, so rent from a home abroad goes on your Australian return, usually with a credit for tax paid abroad.

### The steps to buy in Denmark

- Check if you need permission
- Get a Danish tax number
- Set a budget with a bank
- Make an offer and sign with conditions
- Let your lawyer check the documents
- Register the deed

[The full guide, step by step](https://realhunt.co/guide/denmark)

## Can an Australian buy property in the Dominican Republic?

Short answer: Yes.

Yes. Australians have the same rights as Dominican citizens to buy land and homes, with no restrictions.

General information, not legal advice. Updated November 2026.

### What it costs to buy

About 4.25-7% on top of the price. On a €150,000 home that is €6,375 to €10,500, so €156,375 to €160,500 in total.

The buyer pays a 3% transfer tax (0% for qualifying first purchases under CONFOTUR tourism incentives), legal fees of about 1-2% and notary fees of about 0.25-1%, plus registration costs, while the seller pays the 2-3% agent fee.

[Work it out for your price](https://realhunt.co/buying-costs/dominican-republic)

### Every year

Yearly property tax: The yearly IPI tax is 1% of the part of a person's total Dominican property value, as assessed by the tax office DGII, above RD$10,695,494 in 2026, so a single cheap home is often below the threshold.

Most single homes under about $150,000 pay no IPI property tax because they fall under the threshold, but expect condo fees, utilities and upkeep. A 2026 tax law (Law 30-26) sets a 10% tax on gains when an individual sells, though its regulations were still in draft in October 2026.

Tax on rental income: Rent paid abroad to a non-resident is generally subject to 27% withholding.

### Living there

Buying a home does not by itself give you residency in the Dominican Republic.

### Good to know as an Australian

- Australian tax residents are taxed on worldwide income, so rent from a home abroad goes on your Australian return, usually with a credit for tax paid abroad.

### The steps to buy in the Dominican Republic

- Get a tax ID (RNC)
- Check the title
- Sign a promise of sale
- Sign the deed before a notary
- Pay the transfer tax
- Register the title

[The full guide, step by step](https://realhunt.co/guide/dominican-republic)

## Can an Australian buy property in France?

Short answer: Yes.

Yes. Australians can buy property in France without restrictions and need no permit.

General information, not legal advice. Updated November 2026.

### What it costs to buy

About 7-8.5% on top of the price. On a €150,000 home that is €10,500 to €12,750, so €160,500 to €162,750 in total.

Transfer taxes (droits de mutation) of about 5.8%, or about 6.3% in departments that raised their rate for 2025 to March 2028; notary fee (émoluments) on a sliding scale from 3.87% down to 0.799% plus 20% VAT, about 1.3% on a €150,000 home; land security contribution (contribution de sécurité immobilière) 0.10%; disbursements (débours) of about €800 to €1,200; the agent fee is usually built into the advertised price (FAI) and paid by the seller, sometimes shared.

[Work it out for your price](https://realhunt.co/buying-costs/france)

### Every year

Yearly property tax: Owners pay an annual property tax (taxe foncière) set by the local authorities, and owners of a furnished second home also pay housing tax (taxe d'habitation), which some communes raise by a surcharge of 5% to 60%.

Expect the annual taxe foncière, plus taxe d'habitation if the home is a furnished second home, and income tax and social charges on any rent.

Tax on rental income: Non-residents pay French income tax on French rental income at a minimum rate of 20% (30% above about €27,500), plus social charges of 17.2%, or 7.5% for people covered by social security in another EU/EEA country or Switzerland.

### Living there

Buying a home gives no right to live in France; stays over 90 days need a long-stay visa.

France is in the Schengen area: with an Australian passport you can usually stay up to 90 days in any 180 days across the whole area without a visa.

### Good to know as an Australian

- Australian tax residents are taxed on worldwide income, so rent from a home abroad goes on your Australian return, usually with a credit for tax paid abroad.

### The steps to buy in France

- Make an offer
- Sign the preliminary contract
- Use the cooling-off period
- Pay the deposit
- Let the notary run checks
- Sign the final deed

[The full guide, step by step](https://realhunt.co/guide/france)

## Can an Australian buy property in Germany?

Short answer: Yes.

Yes. There are no restrictions on Australians buying property in Germany, though banks usually ask non-EU buyers for a bigger down payment.

General information, not legal advice. Updated November 2026.

### What it costs to buy

About 5-8.5% on top of the price. On a €150,000 home that is €7,500 to €12,750, so €157,500 to €162,750 in total.

Real estate transfer tax (Grunderwerbsteuer) of 3.5% to 6.5% depending on the state (3.5% in Bavaria, 6.5% in Brandenburg, North Rhine-Westphalia, Saarland and Schleswig-Holstein), plus notary and land registry fees (Notar- und Grundbuchkosten) of about 1.5-2%; if the seller hired the agent, the buyer pays half the commission by law, which is extra.

[Work it out for your price](https://realhunt.co/buying-costs/germany)

### Every year

Yearly property tax: Owners pay property tax (Grundsteuer), calculated since 2025 as assessed value x a tax rate x a municipal multiplier (Hebesatz) that each municipality sets.

Expect the municipal property tax, insurance, utilities and upkeep. Rental profit is taxable in Germany, so a non-resident landlord deals with a German tax office.

Tax on rental income: Non-resident owners are taxed in Germany on net rental income at the normal progressive income tax rates, but without the basic tax-free allowance (Grundfreibetrag).

### Living there

Buying a home gives no right to live in Germany.

Germany is in the Schengen area: with an Australian passport you can usually stay up to 90 days in any 180 days across the whole area without a visa.

### Good to know as an Australian

- Australian tax residents are taxed on worldwide income, so rent from a home abroad goes on your Australian return, usually with a credit for tax paid abroad.

### The steps to buy in Germany

- Find a home and arrange money
- Get independent advice
- Sign before a notary
- Secure a priority notice
- Pay the transfer tax and the price
- Get registered as owner

[The full guide, step by step](https://realhunt.co/guide/germany)

## Can an Australian buy property in Greece?

Short answer: Yes, with conditions.

Yes, with one condition: Australians need a permit to buy in designated border areas (parts of northern Greece and eastern Aegean islands such as Rhodes and the Dodecanese). Elsewhere you buy like a Greek. The government has also announced a 15% transfer tax for non-EU buyers from 1 January 2027, not yet final.

General information, not legal advice. Updated November 2026.

### What it costs to buy

About 5.5-7% on top of the price. On a €150,000 home that is €8,250 to €10,500, so €158,250 to €160,500 in total.

Transfer tax 3.09% of the price or the taxable value, whichever is higher; notary about 0.8-1% plus VAT; land registry fees about 0.5-0.7%; lawyer 1-2% plus VAT; if an agent is used, the buyer usually pays a commission of 1-3% plus VAT on top.

[Work it out for your price](https://realhunt.co/buying-costs/greece)

### Every year

Yearly property tax: Owners on 1 January pay the unified property tax (ENFIA), calculated per property from its location, size, age and official zone value, with an extra charge if total Greek property exceeds €500,000.

Yearly costs are ENFIA and income tax on any rent.

Tax on rental income: Non-residents pay Greek tax on Greek rental income at 15% up to €12,000, 25% to €24,000, 35% to €36,000 and 45% above, after a flat 5% deduction for expenses.

### Living there

Greece has a golden visa for non-EU buyers. Since 2024 the minimum is €800,000 in Attica, Thessaloniki, Mykonos, Santorini and larger islands, and €400,000 elsewhere, so a cheap home does not qualify.

Greece is in the Schengen area: with an Australian passport you can usually stay up to 90 days in any 180 days across the whole area without a visa.

### Good to know as an Australian

- Australian tax residents are taxed on worldwide income, so rent from a home abroad goes on your Australian return, usually with a credit for tax paid abroad.

### The steps to buy in Greece

- Get a Greek tax number
- Hire a lawyer
- Check the title
- Sign a private agreement
- Pay the transfer tax
- Sign the deed and register it

[The full guide, step by step](https://realhunt.co/guide/greece)

### Questions

#### Can an Australian buy property in Greece?

Yes, with one condition: Australians need a permit to buy in designated border areas (parts of northern Greece and eastern Aegean islands such as Rhodes and the Dodecanese). Elsewhere you buy like a Greek. The government has also announced a 15% transfer tax for non-EU buyers from 1 January 2027, not yet final.

#### How much are the buying costs in Greece?

About 5.5-7% on top of the price, so €8,250 to €10,500 on a €150,000 home. Transfer tax 3.09% of the price or the taxable value, whichever is higher; notary about 0.8-1% plus VAT; land registry fees about 0.5-0.7%; lawyer 1-2% plus VAT; if an agent is used, the buyer usually pays a commission of 1-3% plus VAT on top.

#### Is there a yearly property tax in Greece?

Owners on 1 January pay the unified property tax (ENFIA), calculated per property from its location, size, age and official zone value, with an extra charge if total Greek property exceeds €500,000.

#### What tax do I pay on rent in Greece if I live abroad?

Non-residents pay Greek tax on Greek rental income at 15% up to €12,000, 25% to €24,000, 35% to €36,000 and 45% above, after a flat 5% deduction for expenses.

#### Does buying a home in Greece let me live there as an Australian?

Greece has a golden visa for non-EU buyers. Since 2024 the minimum is €800,000 in Attica, Thessaloniki, Mykonos, Santorini and larger islands, and €400,000 elsewhere, so a cheap home does not qualify. Greece is in the Schengen area: with an Australian passport you can usually stay up to 90 days in any 180 days across the whole area without a visa.

## Can an Australian buy property in Italy?

Short answer: Yes.

Yes. Italy lets non-EU citizens buy when their country lets Italians buy (reciprocity), and the US, UK, Canada, Australia and Switzerland all qualify. You need an Italian tax code (codice fiscale).

General information, not legal advice. Updated November 2026.

### What it costs to buy

About 4-15% on top of the price. On a €150,000 home that is €6,000 to €22,500, so €156,000 to €172,500 in total.

Registration tax 9% on a second home (resale), or VAT on new builds; notary 1-2% + legal ~1% + agent ~3% (GPG roundtrip 10-18%).

[Work it out for your price](https://realhunt.co/buying-costs/italy)

### Every year

Yearly property tax: IMU 0.4-1.06% on second homes (on cadastral value).

IMU (council property tax) on second homes and a local waste tax (TARI). For small rural houses these are often a few hundred euros a year.

Tax on rental income: Optional flat 'cedolare secca' on short lets: 21% for one property, 26% from the second.

### Living there

Buying a home gives no right to live in Italy; stays over 90 days need a visa, such as the elective residence visa.

Italy is in the Schengen area: with an Australian passport you can usually stay up to 90 days in any 180 days across the whole area without a visa.

### Good to know as an Australian

- Australian tax residents are taxed on worldwide income, so rent from a home abroad goes on your Australian return, usually with a credit for tax paid abroad.

### The steps to buy in Italy

- Get a codice fiscale
- Make a written offer
- Check the house
- Sign at the notary
- Pay the taxes

[The full guide, step by step](https://realhunt.co/guide/italy)

## Can an Australian buy property in Japan?

Short answer: Yes.

Yes. Australians can buy freehold land and homes on the same terms as Japanese citizens, even on a tourist visa.

General information, not legal advice. Updated November 2026.

### What it costs to buy

About 6-9% on top of the price. On a €150,000 home that is €9,000 to €13,500, so €159,000 to €163,500 in total.

The buyer pays an agent fee capped at 3% plus ¥60,000 plus 10% consumption tax (with a special cap of up to ¥330,000 including tax for cheap vacant homes up to ¥8 million), registration tax of 1.5% on land (until March 2029) and 2% standard on the building, real estate acquisition tax of 3% of assessed value, stamp duty, and a judicial scrivener fee of about ¥100,000 to ¥200,000.

[Work it out for your price](https://realhunt.co/buying-costs/japan)

### Every year

Yearly property tax: Fixed asset tax is 1.4% of the government's assessed value, plus city planning tax of up to 0.3% in urban areas, and small residential plots get a lower tax base.

Expect fixed asset tax of 1.4% and city planning tax of up to 0.3% of assessed value, which is usually well below market value. Add the cost of a tax representative and, for apartments, monthly management and repair fund fees.

Tax on rental income: Rent paid to a non-resident is subject to 20.42% withholding (except when an individual rents it as their own home), and the owner must file a tax return each year through a tax representative in Japan to settle the final tax.

### Living there

Buying a home gives no visa or residency in Japan.

### Good to know as an Australian

- Australian tax residents are taxed on worldwide income, so rent from a home abroad goes on your Australian return, usually with a credit for tax paid abroad.

### The steps to buy in Japan

- Find a home and agent
- Submit a written offer
- Hear the property explanation
- Sign and pay a deposit
- Pay and register
- File reports and name a tax representative

[The full guide, step by step](https://realhunt.co/guide/japan)

## Can an Australian buy property in Mexico?

Short answer: Yes, with conditions.

Yes, with conditions. In the Restricted Zone (within 50 km of the coast or 100 km of the borders, which covers Tulum and Playa del Carmen) Australians buy through a fideicomiso bank trust or a Mexican company. Inland you can own directly, with a permit from the Foreign Ministry.

General information, not legal advice. Updated November 2026.

### What it costs to buy

About 3.5-8% on top of the price. On a €150,000 home that is €5,250 to €12,000, so €155,250 to €162,000 in total.

Acquisition tax 2-5% + notary 0.5-1% + legal 1-1.5% (GPG 3.5-7.5%), plus 0.5-1.5% for fideicomiso/permit setup; TheLatinvestor budgets 5-8%.

[Work it out for your price](https://realhunt.co/buying-costs/mexico)

### Every year

Yearly property tax: Municipal predial, set locally on cadastral value; usually small, often less than HOA fees.

Yearly costs include the local property tax (predial), usually 0.05% to 1.2% of the official cadastral value, which is often well below market value. In the restricted zone add the bank trust fee, about US$450 to US$1,000 a year, plus HOA fees, insurance and upkeep.

Tax on rental income: Non-residents: 25% ISR withholding on gross rent; plus 16% IVA on short-term stays (Airbnb remits on its bookings).

### Living there

Buying a home gives no residency in Mexico; temporary residency is usually based on income or savings and applied for at a Mexican consulate.

### Good to know as an Australian

- Australian tax residents are taxed on worldwide income, so rent from a home abroad goes on your Australian return, usually with a credit for tax paid abroad.

### The steps to buy in Mexico

- Check the restricted zone
- Choose how to hold title
- Check the title
- Sign the purchase contract
- Close with a notary
- Register the deed

[The full guide, step by step](https://realhunt.co/guide/mexico)

## Can an Australian buy property in the Netherlands?

Short answer: Yes.

Yes. There are no nationality or residence rules and no surcharge for foreign buyers in the Netherlands. Some cities restrict renting out cheaper homes after you buy (opkoopbescherming).

General information, not legal advice. Updated November 2026.

### What it costs to buy

About 2-9% on top of the price. On a €150,000 home that is €3,000 to €13,500, so €153,000 to €163,500 in total.

Transfer tax (overdrachtsbelasting) of 8% if you will not live in the home, such as a buy-to-let or holiday home, or 2% if it becomes your main home; a notary fee for the transfer deed of around EUR 500; Kadaster registration fees; and mortgage costs if you borrow; the seller pays its own agent.

[Work it out for your price](https://realhunt.co/buying-costs/netherlands)

### Every year

Yearly property tax: Owners pay municipal property tax (onroerendezaakbelasting, OZB) on the official WOZ value, at a rate each municipality sets, which in practice is a per mille figure; tenants of homes do not pay it.

Expect municipal property tax (OZB), insurance and upkeep, and in a flat the owners' association (VvE) contribution. Non-residents also pay box 3 income tax based on the property's value.

Tax on rental income: Non-residents declare Dutch property in box 3, where tax is 36% on a deemed return of 6% of the property's value in 2026, after a tax-free allowance of EUR 59,357 per person, regardless of actual rent.

### Living there

Buying a home gives no right to live in the Netherlands.

The Netherlands is in the Schengen area: with an Australian passport you can usually stay up to 90 days in any 180 days across the whole area without a visa.

### Good to know as an Australian

- Australian tax residents are taxed on worldwide income, so rent from a home abroad goes on your Australian return, usually with a credit for tax paid abroad.

### The steps to buy in the Netherlands

- Get a BSN
- Set up payment and money
- Make an offer
- Use the 3-day cooling-off period
- Pay the deposit
- Sign the deed and register

[The full guide, step by step](https://realhunt.co/guide/netherlands)

## Can an Australian buy property in Norway?

Short answer: Yes.

Yes. Anyone with the funds can buy property in Norway, and a built plot of up to 2 decares normally needs no concession (konsesjon). Farms and larger plots need a concession.

General information, not legal advice. Updated November 2026.

### What it costs to buy

About 2.5-3% on top of the price. On a €150,000 home that is €3,750 to €4,500, so €153,750 to €154,500 in total.

Document duty (dokumentavgift) of 2.5% of market value, a registration fee (tinglysingsgebyr) of NOK 545 for the deed and NOK 545 for any mortgage document; a flat in a housing cooperative (borettslag) has no document duty; the seller normally pays the agent.

[Work it out for your price](https://realhunt.co/buying-costs/norway)

### Every year

Yearly property tax: Some municipalities charge property tax (eiendomsskatt), at most 4 per mille of the value after a reduction of at least 30%, and some also give a basic deduction; many charge nothing.

Expect municipal property tax where it applies, municipal fees, insurance and upkeep. Costs such as municipal fees and property tax are deductible against rental income.

Tax on rental income: Rental profit is normally taxed at 22%, and the Tax Administration says its rental rules also apply to owners who are tax resident abroad.

### Living there

Buying a home gives no right to live in Norway.

Norway is in the Schengen area: with an Australian passport you can usually stay up to 90 days in any 180 days across the whole area without a visa.

### Good to know as an Australian

- Australian tax residents are taxed on worldwide income, so rent from a home abroad goes on your Australian return, usually with a credit for tax paid abroad.

### The steps to buy in Norway

- Find a home and get loan approval
- Bid through the agent
- Sign the contract
- Pay at settlement
- Get a D-number if needed
- Register the deed

## Can an Australian buy property in Poland?

Short answer: Yes, with conditions.

Partly: Australians can buy an apartment without a permit, but usually need a permit from the Ministry of the Interior (MSWiA) to buy a house or land.

General information, not legal advice. Updated November 2026.

### What it costs to buy

About 2.5-4% on top of the price. On a €150,000 home that is €3,750 to €6,000, so €153,750 to €156,000 in total.

Tax on civil law transactions (PCC) 2% of the value, paid by the buyer within 14 days of the deed; notary fee (taksa notarialna) capped at PLN 1,010 plus 0.4% of the value above PLN 60,000, plus 23% VAT; court fee of PLN 200 to enter ownership in the land register (plus PLN 100 for a new register); optional lawyer about 1%; the agent fee (about 2-3%) depends on the agreement.

[Work it out for your price](https://realhunt.co/buying-costs/poland)

### Every year

Yearly property tax: Owners pay a local property tax (podatek od nieruchomości) set by the commune, capped in 2026 at PLN 1.25 per m² of usable floor space for flats and houses.

Yearly costs are the local property tax, which is low for flats, plus income tax on any rent.

Tax on rental income: Private rental income is taxed as a flat lump sum (ryczałt) of 8.5% of revenue up to PLN 100,000 a year and 12.5% above that.

### Living there

Buying a home gives no right to live in Poland.

Poland is in the Schengen area: with an Australian passport you can usually stay up to 90 days in any 180 days across the whole area without a visa.

### Good to know as an Australian

- Australian tax residents are taxed on worldwide income, so rent from a home abroad goes on your Australian return, usually with a credit for tax paid abroad.

### The steps to buy in Poland

- Get a PESEL number
- Check if you need a permit
- Sign a preliminary agreement
- Do due diligence
- Sign the notarial deed
- Pay the PCC tax

[The full guide, step by step](https://realhunt.co/guide/poland)

## Can an Australian buy property in Portugal?

Short answer: Yes.

Yes. Australians buy in Portugal with the same rights as Portuguese citizens. You need a Portuguese tax number (NIF).

General information, not legal advice. Updated November 2026.

### What it costs to buy

About 3-12% on top of the price. On a €150,000 home that is €4,500 to €18,000, so €154,500 to €168,000 in total.

IMT transfer tax 0-8% (progressive) + stamp duty 0.8% + notary/registry 0.9-1.2% + legal 1.25-2%.

[Work it out for your price](https://realhunt.co/buying-costs/portugal)

### Every year

Yearly property tax: IMI 0.3-0.45% of taxable value (urban), set by municipality.

IMI (council tax), usually 0.3–0.45% of the tax value for urban property.

Tax on rental income: Long-term: 25% flat for non-residents; short-term (AL) under the simplified regime only 35-50% of gross is taxable.

### Living there

Since October 2023, buying a home no longer qualifies for Portugal's golden visa. The D7 visa for people with passive income is the usual route to live there.

Portugal is in the Schengen area: with an Australian passport you can usually stay up to 90 days in any 180 days across the whole area without a visa.

### Good to know as an Australian

- Australian tax residents are taxed on worldwide income, so rent from a home abroad goes on your Australian return, usually with a credit for tax paid abroad.

## Can an Australian buy property in Spain?

Short answer: Yes.

Yes, for now. Australians buy in Spain on the same terms as Spaniards and need an NIE, the foreigner tax number. The government has proposed a 100% tax on (or a ban for) non-EU buyers who do not live in Spain; it is not law as of November 2026, so check before you sign.

General information, not legal advice. Updated November 2026.

### What it costs to buy

About 7.5-14% on top of the price. On a €150,000 home that is €11,250 to €21,000, so €161,250 to €171,000 in total.

New build: 10% IVA + 0.5-1.5% AJD stamp duty + notary 0.5-1% + legal 1-2%; resale: ITP transfer tax 6-11% instead of IVA/AJD.

[Work it out for your price](https://realhunt.co/buying-costs/spain)

### Every year

Yearly property tax: IBI 0.4-1.1% of cadastral value (municipal), plus imputed income tax on unlet homes.

IBI (council tax) and waste collection. Non-residents who do not rent the house out also file a small yearly imputed-income tax.

Tax on rental income: Non-residents: EU/EEA 19% on net income; non-EU 24% on gross with no deductions.

### Living there

Buying a home gives no right to live in Spain: the golden visa for property buyers closed on 3 April 2025. The non-lucrative visa is the usual route for people with passive income.

Spain is in the Schengen area: with an Australian passport you can usually stay up to 90 days in any 180 days across the whole area without a visa.

### Good to know as an Australian

- Australian tax residents are taxed on worldwide income, so rent from a home abroad goes on your Australian return, usually with a credit for tax paid abroad.

### The steps to buy in Spain

- Get an NIE
- Open a Spanish bank account
- Reserve with an arras contract
- Check the house
- Sign at the notary and register
- Pay the transfer tax

## Can an Australian buy property in Sweden?

Short answer: Yes.

Yes. There are no citizenship or residence rules for buying a home in Sweden. You need a Swedish personal identity number or a coordination number (samordningsnummer) to register ownership.

General information, not legal advice. Updated November 2026.

### What it costs to buy

About 1.5-3.5% on top of the price. On a €150,000 home that is €2,250 to €5,250, so €152,250 to €155,250 in total.

Stamp duty on the title (lagfart) of 1.5% of the price or tax value, whichever is higher, plus a SEK 825 fee; if you borrow and need new mortgage deeds (pantbrev), 2% of their amount plus a SEK 375 fee; optional legal advice; the seller normally pays the agent, and a cooperative flat (bostadsrätt) has no lagfart.

[Work it out for your price](https://realhunt.co/buying-costs/sweden)

### Every year

Yearly property tax: Houses pay a municipal property fee (kommunal fastighetsavgift) of SEK 10,425 in 2026, or 0.75% of the tax value if that is lower.

House owners pay the municipal property fee and must file a Swedish tax return if they owe it or have rental income, even when living abroad. Add insurance, utilities and upkeep.

Tax on rental income: Non-resident individuals pay 30% tax on net rental income as capital income; for a private home you can first deduct SEK 40,000 per property and 20% of the rent (the 20% does not apply to a bostadsrätt).

### Living there

Buying a home gives no right to live in Sweden.

Sweden is in the Schengen area: with an Australian passport you can usually stay up to 90 days in any 180 days across the whole area without a visa.

### Good to know as an Australian

- Australian tax residents are taxed on worldwide income, so rent from a home abroad goes on your Australian return, usually with a credit for tax paid abroad.

### The steps to buy in Sweden

- Get a coordination number
- Open a Swedish bank account
- Find a home and arrange money
- Inspect before you commit
- Sign the purchase contract
- Apply for title at Lantmäteriet

[The full guide, step by step](https://realhunt.co/guide/sweden)

## Can an Australian buy property in Switzerland?

Short answer: Restricted.

Restricted. Under the Lex Koller law, Australians living abroad need a cantonal permit and can usually only buy one holiday home in a tourist area, within national quotas. Living in Switzerland, holders of a C permit buy like Swiss citizens, and holders of a B permit can buy the home they live in.

General information, not legal advice. Updated November 2026.

### What it costs to buy

About 1-5% on top of the price. On a €150,000 home that is €1,500 to €7,500, so €151,500 to €157,500 in total.

Transfer tax (Handänderungssteuer, droits de mutation) 0% to about 3.3% depending on the canton; notary about 0.1-0.5%; land register fee, a small fixed amount or percentage; optional lawyer 1-2%; the agent fee (2-3%) is paid by the seller.

[Work it out for your price](https://realhunt.co/buying-costs/switzerland)

### Every year

Yearly property tax: More than half of the cantons charge an annual property tax (Liegenschaftssteuer), usually 0.01-0.3% of the assessed value, and owners also pay cantonal wealth tax on the property value minus the mortgage.

Yearly costs are wealth tax, cantonal property tax where it exists, and tax on imputed rental value (Eigenmietwert) if you use the home yourself. Imputed rental value is due to end on 1 January 2029, and cantons may then add a new tax on second homes.

Tax on rental income: Non-residents pay tax on net Swiss rental income at ordinary cantonal and communal rates plus federal direct tax, and some cantons set the rate using worldwide income.

### Living there

Buying a home gives no right to live in Switzerland.

Switzerland is in the Schengen area: with an Australian passport you can usually stay up to 90 days in any 180 days across the whole area without a visa.

### Good to know as an Australian

- Australian tax residents are taxed on worldwide income, so rent from a home abroad goes on your Australian return, usually with a credit for tax paid abroad.

### The steps to buy in Switzerland

- Check your Lex Koller status
- Arrange financing
- Find a property and make an offer
- Sign the deed at a notary
- Register the transfer

[The full guide, step by step](https://realhunt.co/guide/switzerland)

## Can an Australian buy property in the United Kingdom?

Short answer: Yes.

Yes. There are no nationality restrictions on buying homes anywhere in the UK. In England and Northern Ireland, buyers who do not live in the UK pay a 2% stamp duty surcharge.

General information, not legal advice. Updated November 2026.

### What it costs to buy

About 3-9% on top of the price. On a €150,000 home that is €4,500 to €13,500, so €154,500 to €163,500 in total.

In England and Northern Ireland, Stamp Duty Land Tax (SDLT) is 0% up to £125,000 and 2% from £125,001 to £250,000, plus a 2% surcharge for non-UK residents and a further 5% if you already own a home anywhere, so a non-resident who owns another home pays 7% up to £125,000 and 9% to £250,000; solicitor (conveyancer) about 0.6-1% with a typical minimum of around £2,100 including VAT; Land Registry fee £20 to £230; searches extra; the seller pays the estate agent.

[Work it out for your price](https://realhunt.co/buying-costs/united-kingdom)

### Every year

Yearly property tax: Owners or occupiers pay council tax to the local council, and many councils in England charge second homes a premium of up to 100% from April 2025.

Yearly costs are council tax, which may include a second home premium, plus a self assessment tax return and income tax if you let the home.

Tax on rental income: Non-resident landlords pay UK income tax on rent at 20%, 40% or 45%, with 20% deducted at source by the agent or tenant unless HMRC approves gross payment, and the rates on property income are set to rise to 22%, 42% and 47% from April 2027.

### Living there

Buying a home gives no right to live in the UK. Visitors can usually stay up to 6 months, and most now need an electronic travel authorisation (ETA) before they travel.

### Good to know as an Australian

- Australian tax residents are taxed on worldwide income, so rent from a home abroad goes on your Australian return, usually with a credit for tax paid abroad.

### The steps to buy in the United Kingdom

- Make an offer
- Instruct a solicitor
- Run searches and enquiries
- Exchange contracts
- Complete
- Pay SDLT and register

[The full guide, step by step](https://realhunt.co/guide/united-kingdom)

#### Can foreigners buy a house in Canada?

Mostly not for now: a federal ban stops non-Canadians from buying homes in cities and larger towns until January 1, 2027, with exceptions such as work permit holders and spouses of citizens or permanent residents. The ban does not cover rural areas and small towns, and the government has said it does not plan simply to extend it, but a replacement is being studied.

#### What are the buying costs in Canada?

Plan for about 1.5-4% on top of the price: Buyers usually pay provincial land transfer tax on a sliding scale (Ontario: 0.5% up to $55,000 and 1% from $55,000 to $250,000), legal fees of about $500 to $1,500, title insurance of about $250 and an inspection of $300 to $1,000, while the seller usually pays the agents; foreign buyers also pay Ontario's 25% non-resident speculation tax anywhere in Ontario and British Columbia's 20% additional tax in Metro Vancouver and four other regions.. This is general information, not tax advice.

No. RealHunt is not an estate agent. Every home links to its original listing, so you deal directly with the seller or agent.

#### How much does a cheap house cost in Cyprus?

Ready 2-bed flat steps from the beach in Coral Bay, with pool and sea views, in Coral Bay, Paphos, for €341,000, with a RealHunt score of 93. The list is updated as new homes pass our check.

#### Can foreigners buy a house in Cyprus?

EU citizens buy without restrictions. Non-EU buyers need permission from the Council of Ministers, applied for through the District Officer, and are normally limited to one home or a plot of up to 4,014 m².

#### What are the buying costs in Cyprus?

Plan for about 2.5-3.5% on top of the price: Land Registry transfer fees of 3% up to €85,000, 5% to €170,000 and 8% above, halved for resales without VAT (1.5%, 2.5% and 4%); stamp duty abolished from 1 January 2026; lawyer about 1% plus VAT; small Land Registry charges.. This is general information, not tax advice.

### Questions about buying in Denmark

#### How much does a cheap house cost in Denmark?

On RealHunt the homes in Denmark start at €35,400. The median price is €93,200 and the median price per square metre is €787, across 45 homes checked by a person.

#### Which is the best-rated home in Denmark right now?

198 m² family villa near the Limfjord for under €80k, in Ranum, North Jutland, for €79,800, with a RealHunt score of 98. The list is updated as new homes pass our check.

#### Can foreigners buy a house in Denmark?

Without Danish domicile or 5 years of past residence you need permission from the Department of Civil Affairs (Civilstyrelsen); EU/EEA citizens who live and are registered in Denmark can buy a permanent home without permission by signing a declaration to the Land Registration Court. Holiday homes (sommerhuse) need permission, which is only given to people with particularly strong ties to Denmark, such as many years of holidays there.

#### What are the buying costs in Denmark?

Plan for about 1.5-3% on top of the price: Registration fee on the deed (tinglysningsafgift) of DKK 1,850 plus 0.6% of the price, about 1% for a buyer's lawyer, and, if you borrow, a mortgage registration fee of DKK 1,825 plus 1.25% of the loan; the seller normally pays the agent.. This is general information, not tax advice.

#### Does RealHunt sell these homes?

### Questions about buying in Dominican Republic

#### How much does a cheap house cost in Dominican Republic?

On RealHunt the homes in Dominican Republic start at €187,800. The median price is €223,600 and the median price per square metre is €2,282, across 4 homes checked by a person.

#### Which is the best-rated home in Dominican Republic right now?

Oceanfront 3-bed flat in Juan Dolio with wide Caribbean views, in Juan Dolio, San Pedro de Macorís, for €223,600, with a RealHunt score of 90. The list is updated as new homes pass our check.

#### Can foreigners buy a house in Dominican Republic?

Yes. Foreigners have the same rights as Dominican citizens to buy land and homes, with no restrictions.

#### What are the buying costs in Dominican Republic?

Plan for about 4.25-7% on top of the price: The buyer pays a 3% transfer tax (0% for qualifying first purchases under CONFOTUR tourism incentives), legal fees of about 1-2% and notary fees of about 0.25-1%, plus registration costs, while the seller pays the 2-3% agent fee.. This is general information, not tax advice.

#### Does RealHunt sell these homes?

No. RealHunt is not an estate agent. Every home links to its original listing, so you deal directly with the seller or agent.

### Questions about buying in France

#### How much does a cheap house cost in France?

On RealHunt the homes in France start at €39,000. The median price is €59,000 and the median price per square metre is €1,154, across 32 homes checked by a person.

#### Which is the best-rated home in France right now?

171 m² house with a former shop in the centre of Bussière-Poitevine, in Bussière-Poitevine, Haute-Vienne, for €39,950, with a RealHunt score of 92. The list is updated as new homes pass our check.

#### Can foreigners buy a house in France?

Yes. Foreigners can buy property in France without major restrictions, and non-EU buyers do not need a permit, although the paperwork can take longer.

#### What are the buying costs in France?

Plan for about 7-8.5% on top of the price: Transfer taxes (droits de mutation) of about 5.8%, or about 6.3% in departments that raised their rate for 2025 to March 2028; notary fee (émoluments) on a sliding scale from 3.87% down to 0.799% plus 20% VAT, about 1.3% on a €150,000 home; land security contribution (contribution de sécurité immobilière) 0.10%; disbursements (débours) of about €800 to €1,200; the agent fee is usually built into the advertised price (FAI) and paid by the seller, sometimes shared.. This is general information, not tax advice.

#### Does RealHunt sell these homes?

No. RealHunt is not an estate agent. Every home links to its original listing, so you deal directly with the seller or agent.

### Questions about buying in Germany

#### How much does a cheap house cost in Germany?

On RealHunt the homes in Germany start at €40,000. The median price is €55,000 and the median price per square metre is €1,053, across 20 homes checked by a person.

#### Which is the best-rated home in Germany right now?

Sunny attic flat with a balcony for €40,000 in Chemnitz, in Ebersdorf, Chemnitz, for €40,000, with a RealHunt score of 87. The list is updated as new homes pass our check.

#### Can foreigners buy a house in Germany?

Yes. There are no restrictions on foreigners buying property in Germany, though non-EU buyers usually need a bigger down payment to get a loan.

#### What are the buying costs in Germany?

Plan for about 5-8.5% on top of the price: Real estate transfer tax (Grunderwerbsteuer) of 3.5% to 6.5% depending on the state (3.5% in Bavaria, 6.5% in Brandenburg, North Rhine-Westphalia, Saarland and Schleswig-Holstein), plus notary and land registry fees (Notar- und Grundbuchkosten) of about 1.5-2%; if the seller hired the agent, the buyer pays half the commission by law, which is extra.. This is general information, not tax advice.

#### Does RealHunt sell these homes?

No. RealHunt is not an estate agent. Every home links to its original listing, so you deal directly with the seller or agent.

### Questions about buying in Greece

#### How much does a cheap house cost in Greece?

On RealHunt the homes in Greece start at €68,000. The median price is €115,000 and the median price per square metre is €1,397, across 14 homes checked by a person.

#### Which is the best-rated home in Greece right now?

Three-bedroom village house with a vine-covered terrace and sea views in Messinia, in Vasilitsi, Messinia, for €109,000, with a RealHunt score of 93. The list is updated as new homes pass our check.

#### Can foreigners buy a house in Greece?

Yes. Buyers from outside the EU and EFTA need a permit to buy in designated border areas (parts of northern Greece and eastern Aegean islands such as the Dodecanese and Rhodes). The government has announced a 15% transfer tax for non-EU buyers of homes from 1 January 2027, not yet final in September 2026.

#### What are the buying costs in Greece?

Plan for about 5.5-7% on top of the price: Transfer tax 3.09% of the price or the taxable value, whichever is higher; notary about 0.8-1% plus VAT; land registry fees about 0.5-0.7%; lawyer 1-2% plus VAT; if an agent is used, the buyer usually pays a commission of 1-3% plus VAT on top.. This is general information, not tax advice.

#### Does RealHunt sell these homes?

No. RealHunt is not an estate agent. Every home links to its original listing, so you deal directly with the seller or agent.

### Questions about buying in Italy

#### How much does a cheap house cost in Italy?

On RealHunt the homes in Italy start at €12,000. The median price is €49,000 and the median price per square metre is €975, across 59 homes checked by a person.

#### Which is the best-rated home in Italy right now?

Renovated stone house with a lake-view balcony above Lake Como, in San Siro, Lake Como, for €95,000, with a RealHunt score of 91. The list is updated as new homes pass our check.

#### Can foreigners buy a house in Italy?

Yes for EU citizens; non-EU buyers need reciprocity (US, UK, Canada, Australia qualify).

#### What are the buying costs in Italy?

Plan for about 4-15% on top of the price: Registration tax 9% on a second home (resale), or VAT on new builds; notary 1-2% + legal ~1% + agent ~3% (GPG roundtrip 10-18%).. This is general information, not tax advice.

#### Does RealHunt sell these homes?

No. RealHunt is not an estate agent. Every home links to its original listing, so you deal directly with the seller or agent.

### Questions about buying in Japan

#### How much does a cheap house cost in Japan?

On RealHunt the homes in Japan start at €7,400. The median price is €39,560 and the median price per square metre is €340, across 30 homes checked by a person.

#### Which is the best-rated home in Japan right now?

Furnished log cabin on stilts with a deck in the Hida forest, in Shokawa, Takayama, Gifu, for €11,380, with a RealHunt score of 91. The list is updated as new homes pass our check.

#### Can foreigners buy a house in Japan?

Yes. Foreigners can buy freehold land and homes on the same terms as Japanese citizens, even on a tourist visa, though buying does not give a visa or residency.

#### What are the buying costs in Japan?

Plan for about 6-9% on top of the price: The buyer pays an agent fee capped at 3% plus ¥60,000 plus 10% consumption tax (with a special cap of up to ¥330,000 including tax for cheap vacant homes up to ¥8 million), registration tax of 1.5% on land (until March 2029) and 2% standard on the building, real estate acquisition tax of 3% of assessed value, stamp duty, and a judicial scrivener fee of about ¥100,000 to ¥200,000.. This is general information, not tax advice.

#### Does RealHunt sell these homes?

No. RealHunt is not an estate agent. Every home links to its original listing, so you deal directly with the seller or agent.
